characters.name: Jeff Probst
characters.description: Actually Pretty Funny:At the Final Five Tribal Council inCagayan, Jeff was visibly amused at all theTake Thatsand angry tirades.At the Final Six Tribal Council forBlood vs. Water(a historic vote which led to only the second rock draw in the show's history), he was shown cracking up at Tyson's trolling of Hayden with the suggestion that rustling and ruffling feathers are different things. At the Final Five Tribal Council inCagayan, Jeff was visibly amused at all theTake Thatsand angry tirades. At the Final Six Tribal Council forBlood vs. Water(a historic vote which led to only the second rock draw in the show's history), he was shown cracking up at Tyson's trolling of Hayden with the suggestion that rustling and ruffling feathers are different things. Berserk Button:He's normally pretty level-headed, but if someone quits without good reason, he immediately starts frowning and talking down to them. In his view,Survivoris a difficult environment, but it's one you signed up for and one that the rest of the players manage to handle, so you need to tough it out (or at least leave the game through the normal procedure of having the tribe send you home). When Colton quitBlood vs. Water, he escalated to delivering a full"The Reason You Suck" Speech.note(Though he's more sympathetic if it's a reason beyond simple discomfort, such as having a mental breakdown (Kathy), having a family emergency (Jenna), trying to quit as a gameplay maneuver (Janu), being in too much pain to continue onward (Dana), or having an injury that risks jeopardizing your career (Bi).)He has low tolerance for any disrespect of the pageantry and traditions ofSurvivor. This goes all the way back toBorneo, as the Pagong tribe all wrote Jeff down as their votes at the first Tribal Council, which resulted in him completely losing his shit at them (this never made the show, but was in Mark Burnett's book about the first season). This extends to some of his favorite players, as he was visibly pissed with Colby

characters.name: Pagong
characters.description: Decapitated Army: Tagi purposely targeted Gretchen in their first vote, because she was clearly theTeam Mom. Once she was gone, Pagong becameeasy pickings. Dwindling Party: Both theUr-ExampleandTrope Makerfor Survivor. From Bad to Worse: After Gretchen'sShocking Elimination. Location Theme Naming: Their tribe name was based on the beach they lived on, Pagong. Out of Focus: Get noticeably less screentime during the first episode in comparison to Tagi; over half the tribe aren't even shownspeaking.

characters.name: Tagi
characters.description: Anti-Hero Team: TheUr-ExampleandTrope Makeras the Tagi alliance were the first alliance in Survivor history. Chekhov's Skill: The Pagonging strategy will be used by numerous tribes during the merge in future seasons. Location Theme Naming: Their tribe name was based on the beach they lived on, Tagi. Monochrome Casting: The entire tribe was white. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork

characters.name: Rattana
characters.description: Cerebus Syndrome: Gretchen is the first one out, and if you're part of the audience that hates alliances at the time it only gets nastier...

characters.name: Richard Hatch
characters.description: Richard would return forAll-Stars. Action Survivor: He's noNon-Action Guy, but he's nowhere near the league of physical players like Kelly or/and Greg. Affably Evil: For all his manipulative ruthlessness, he's still a pretty nice guy and is very relatable. Badass Boast:Before he was even officiallycast, here's what he had to say toMark Burnett, Jeff Probst, and Les Moonves:You know you're going to pick me, but what you don't know is that I'm going towin. And after I win, I'm going to hostnextyear's show.Of course, on the very first day of Borneo, he said this:I'm good to go survival-wise. People-wise, it'll be a little more challengin', but I've got the million-dollar check written already. I mean, I'm the winner. It's that kind of cocky attitude that makes people really hate your guts. So, that's the kind of thing I have to keep under wraps.Again, in Episode 9, referring to the last Tribal Council where Sean referred to Richard's fishing as the reason he hasn't been voted out yet:...Catching fish makes people happy, but that's not the reason they're voting me here. They're not voting me off becauseI'm not letting them. Before he was even officiallycast, here's what he had to say toMark Burnett, Jeff Probst, and Les Moonves:You know you're going to pick me, but what you don't know is that I'm going towin. And after I win, I'm going to hostnextyear's show.

characters.name: Kelly Wiglesworth
characters.description: Years after Borneo, Kelly was chosen via a public vote to compete onCambodia. Action Girl: Her impressive streak of immunity challenge wins is the reason she made it to the final, as the Tagi alliance was gunning for her from the moment she defected. Also, Kelly created the record for most individual immunity wins in a single season for womannoteColby Donaldsonbroke her record with 5 wins in a single season.Jenna MosacaandKim Spradlinhad also won four individual immunity challenges during their respective seasons. The Big Girl: To Tagi. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Sean and especially Susan viewed her like this at Final Tribal Council. Cheaters Never Prosper: Richard claimed in post-game interviews that Kelly may have been fed by members of Production at points.

characters.name: Rudolph "Rudy" Boesch
characters.description: Rudy was chosen to compete inAll-Stars. An Offer You Can't Refuse: Would frequently make remarks about what he and his "buddies" would do to anyone that broke ranks from the Tagis. Exactly how many of them were supposed to be taken seriously is aRiddle for the Ages. Breakout Character: While he's still a fan favorite, at the time of the show he wasby farthe most popular contestant due to his humorous personality. Character Development: He originally said he wouldvote out someone for being queer, but then forms his closest alliance and friendship with Richard. Cool Old Guy: The oldest person to appear on the show.

characters.name: Susan "Sue" Hawk
characters.description: Susan was selected to return inAll-Stars. Brutal Honesty: Sue admitted to this. Cluster F-Bomb: During the penultimate episode when she has a falling out with Kelly, Sue falls into this. The DragonorThe Starscream: Depending on what point of the season it is she's either the most ardent supporter of Richard's alliance or planning to backstab him with Kelly. Hair-Trigger Temper: She has her moments.

characters.name: Sean Kenniff
characters.description: Advanced Tech 2000: His (useless) handcrafted fishing pole, which he dubs "The Superpole 2000." Being Good Sucks: He chose to vote alphabetically only because he was trying to find a way to vote that wasn't based on emotional decisions, and thus not upset the person he was voting for. Brainy Brunette: In Real Life. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Sean was a Doctor, specifically a Neurologist and he did treat Sonja's wound. However, his personality and portrayal on the show cause people to question how he was able to become one in the first place. Butt-Monkey: Everyone treated him as either weak or stupid (or both) because of his alphabet strategy.

characters.name: Colleen Haskell
characters.description: Broken Bird: Actually manages to turn into this the further along the season goes post-merge. As it becomes more and more hopeless for Pagong to win it's pretty clear she just wants the whole thing to be over with.In particular, her legs were in a nauseating condition by the time she was voted out, to the point thatbugs were starting to nest in her wounds. In particular, her legs were in a nauseating condition by the time she was voted out, to the point thatbugs were starting to nest in her wounds. Biting-the-Hand Humor: While she does it much less than Greg, she does her fair share of mocking the concept of the show. Break the Cutie: As she watches her tribe get voted out one by one, this happens to her. Deadpan Snarker: Especially with Richard around.

characters.name: Gervase Peterson
characters.description: Many Years after Borneo, Gervase would be selected to return forBlood vs. Waterwithhis niece, Marissa. The Charmer: This was his strategy to winning the game. He made no effort to disguise the fact that he didn't particularly pitch in and help around the camp and instead banked on people finding him entertaining enough to keep around. The Lancer: To Pagong. Late Character Syndrome: Not given any lines or notable screentime until the second episode, an early sign he's not going to win the show. Lazy Bum: Self-Admitted.

characters.name: Jenna Lewis
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: Shii Ann considers her to be one. Broken Bird: SeeTook a Level in Jerkass. Fantastic Racism: Towards previous winners. Four Is Death: Boston Rob cast the fourth and final vote against her. Graceful Loser: Jenna was not bitter because she hadn't been betrayed.

characters.name: Greg(ory) Buis
characters.description: All There in the Manual: In the companion book to the show,Mark Burnettespouses in detail how Greg basically drove the crewnuts. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: "If people are fear and self-preservation motivated they'll band together, they'll form alliances, they'll start beating people out to get rid of the strong ones and get rid of this and get rid of that and, you know, if that happens I hope they vote me off soon because that to me is — whoa, cool flying fish." Badass Bookworm: Attended an Ivy League University, and was one of the best pure survivalists in this or any other season. The Big Guy: To Pagong. Biting-the-Hand Humor: His general mockery of the show, especially the supposed seriousness of Tribal Council, counts as this.

characters.name: Gretchen Cordy
characters.description: Action Mom: Gretchen was a Survival Instructor for the army. Anyone Can Die: The reaction the Pagong tribe (and even the production team) had when Gretchen was voted out. Big "OMG!": At her last tribal council. Death by Pragmatism: Richard said the reason they targeted Gretchen at the merge was that she was the only person on the other tribe with enough life experience and wisdom to keep Pagong unified post-merge. Decoy Protagonist: Had the show remained a test of strength and survival skill as it was originally envisioned, Gretchen the Army Survival Instructor would've had a good chance of winning her season. During her time on the show she portrayed asThe Heroineof the Pagong tribe and the most competent member of it, but as a result became the very first victim of blindside in the show's history. Her refusal to create an alliance, then being voted out for purely pragmatic reasons by the Tagi tribe's own alliance, is perhaps the show'sEstablishing Series Moment.

characters.name: Joel Klug
characters.description: The Cassandra: He was the only person on Pagong who evenconsideredthat forming alliances might be a good idea, and was booted because he was considered "arrogant" for even bringing up the idea. Farm Boy: According to hisBio, Joel grew up in a farm. Out of Focus: Relative to his castmates, Joel didn't get much screentime. The Stinger: During the montage where the women of Pagong proclaim that Joel is a chauvinist, Joel adamantly denies that he is one and says that he thinks that women are equal to men. But at the very end, Joel makes a weird little fluttering movement with his eyes that suggests that maybe he really is one. Straw Misogynist: Maybe. SeeThe Stingerabove.

characters.name: Dirk Been
characters.description: Blind Date: Dirk Mention liked to go out on these in hisPre-Game Profile. Farm Boy: He was a dairy farmer when he came on the show. Hypocrite: A minor example, but Dirk said he was getting annoyed with Rich talking about his homosexuality. Dirk was talking a lot about his Religion and was annoying his tribe (Sue in particular) with his blather while Richard kept quiet about him being gay. Lazy Bum: In the last episode or two that he was in. Precocious Crush: With Kelly. It's actually a little cute once you realize that it genuinelyisjust precocious and not sexual in nature.

characters.name: Ramona Gray
characters.description: Acquitted Too Late: Perceived as lazy at first when in reality it was because she had grown sick from the tropical climate. By the time she had recovered and shown she was more than capable of assisting around camp, the rest of the team had grown too close to possibly save her, leaving her on the bottom during the second vote and getting her eliminated. Audience Surrogate: Shown mere minutes into the game what happens when you throw a normal, average joe into the wilderness and tell them good luck, as sheimmediatelystruggles, and her own inability to adapt to the game is established as her primary narrative. Heel–Face Door-Slam: She was sick for most of the game, but she got better just in time for this to happen. In fact, the episode she was voted off in is entitled "Too Little, Too Late". Lazy Bum: Her tribe accused her of this, when in reality she was simply too sick from the elements to properly contribute. The Load: Ramona's sickness made her weak in challenges and she didn't work around camp until the end.

characters.name: Stacey Stillman
characters.description: Alliterative Name:StaceyStillman. Brainy Brunette: Technically,shewas the first person to start an alliance on Survivor. It was just a failed one, and it only failed allegedly due toExecutive Meddlingand/or Sue to be aWild Card. The Load: Accused of this,in spite of being the reason Tagi won the second challenge.Played Straightin terms of camp life, where Stacey was regularly brought up as slacking around camp in terms of physical work, and her main issue with Rudy was his pushing to work hard on the shelter and collecting food. Played Straightin terms of camp life, where Stacey was regularly brought up as slacking around camp in terms of physical work, and her main issue with Rudy was his pushing to work hard on the shelter and collecting food. Plucky Girl: A rare negative example; Stacey's own optimistic and rather lax view on the survival element in exchange for a higher emphasis on her social game rubbed her tribe the wrong way, especially in the early, "old school" days of Survivor strategy. To her credit, she never stops fighting to try and keep herself in, it just didn't work out that way.

characters.name: Bill Byron "B.B." Andersen
characters.description: Alliterative Name: B.B. is short forBillByron. Benevolent Boss: At least he TRIED to be this. Digging Yourself Deeper: Unlike Rudy, B.B refused to alter his aggressive Type A personality to work with his tribe. Gervase even references this very trope just before Pagong heads to Tribal Council by saying that B.B dug his own grave. Fish Out of Water: B.B. was the oldest member of the youth-dominated Pagong tribe, and his age combined with his abrasive personality didn't let him fit in. Or as best summed up by Greg:Greg: "B.B.'s a good guy. He's pretty strong willed and he's got his plan as well. He's caring. He commands respect. Definitely feels the difference between his age and other people, and doesn't want to seem to bridge that gap as much as just be who he is." Grumpy Old Man: B.B. was upset with tribemates' lack of work ethic.

characters.name: Sonja Christopher
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: Sonja is the oldest woman to complete ever on Survivor and is a very sweet and funny woman. Establishing Character Moment: When she played her parody rendition of "Bye Bye Blues" on her ukulele to Richard. Hide Your Lesbians: Sonja's sexuality wasn't known until well after the show. Inspirationally Disadvantaged: According to herBio, Sonja beat out Cancer. It's All My Fault: Sonja felt responsible for the tribe's loss at the immunity challenge.

characters.name: Ogakor
characters.description: Animal Motif: Crocodiles. Animal Theme Naming: Their name is an aboriginal word for crocodile. Badass Crew: The first of four tribes to produce two winners, with Tina in this season and Amber inAll-Stars.noteThe others are Maaramu fromMarquesas(Vecepia and Boston Rob), Hunahpu fromSan Juan Del Sur(Natalie and Jeremy), and Aparri fromCagayan(Tony and Sarah). Drake fromPearl Islandshas two wins under its belt, but both of these were for the same person.Additionally, Tina, Jerri and Colby all go deep into the game in future seasons, with Tina and Jerri both making it to Day 38 and Colby making it to Day 37, thus making Ogakor one of the most successful tribes in the entire series. Never Smile at a Crocodile: Their tribe name is Okagor, which is an Aboriginal translated version of crocodile.

characters.name: Kucha
characters.description: The Ace: They won a majority of the tribal challenges, even winning three immunity challenges in a row. Animal Motif: Kangaroos. Animal Theme Naming: Their name is an aboriginal word for Kangaroo. Butt-Monkey: They weren't this in the tribal phase as they won the majority of the challenges. But they did become this come the merge after Jeff is voted out. Dwindling Party: Once Jeff is voted out at the merge, Kucha gets decimated, losing all its members after the Final Four.

characters.name: Barramundi
characters.description: Animal Theme Naming: Named for a type of fish.

characters.name: Tina Wesson
characters.description: Tina was chosen to compete onAll-Starsand laterBlood Vs. Waterwith herDaughter, Katie Collins. The Chessmaster: Tina used her knowledge of Debb's vote against Jeff to have the advantage at the merge. Defeating the Undefeatable: Defeated Colby, the favorite to win and unstoppable challenge beast, in a close vote. Epic Fail: In her audition video. Everyone Loves Blondes: Very well-liked and respected by her tribemates. Oh, and she was blonde.

characters.name: Colby Donaldson
characters.description: Colby would return forAll-Starsand laterHeroes vs. Villains. The Ace: Colby set the record for most individual immunity challenges won in a single season with 5, outdoingKelly Wiglesworth'srecord of 4 immunity wins. He was only tied five seasons later by Palau's Tom Westman. Only a few have matched this record since, and zero have surpassed it. Not even his later appearances came close. Baby Name Trend Starter: As explained by Jeff when he returned inHeroes vs. Villains, he inspired a lot of parents to name their children "Colby". Batman Gambit: He pulled one on the Kucha tribe during the first merge round by pretending to be irritating and annoying to get the Kuchas to vote for him instead of Jerri, who had several votes cast against her previously while he had none (this was back when prior votes broke up ties). His tribe also had info that Jeff had prior votes against him from his tribe, so when there was a 5-5 deadlock between Jeff and Colby to leave, Jeff was the one who had his torch extinguished. Being Good Sucks: Had he took Keith with him to the final two he probably would have won, but he disliked Keith and was loyal to Tina.

characters.name: Keith Famie
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Keith was the main target of Jerri’s torment, but once Jerri is gone he becomes Colby’s target. Even Tina admits they kept Keith around because they needed the extra vote. Chef of Iron: Keith was an actual chef and was one of the few people to give Colby a run for his money in the challenges. The Comically Serious: His tiffs with both Jerri and Colby end up being this. The Friend Nobody Likes: Towards the end of the game, it became clear the Ogakor alliance would never be loyal to him. Tina didn't respect him and only saw his value as an extra vote. Colby outright hated him, and put his own chances of winning in jeopardy just to not bring Keith to the finals. The Lancer: To Ogakor.

characters.name: Elisabeth Filarski
characters.description: Delicate and Sickly: Was extremely malnourished in the show, to the extent that her hair was falling out.Though also a bit of a Zig-Zagged example as, by her own admission, there was a period in the Outback when she feltbetterthan she had in a long time, with chronic stomach problems she suffered from disappearing during the game. It was this fact (and the return of her symptoms after her boot,) that helped her and her doctors determine she was suffering from an undiagnosed case of Celiac Disease, and the "Survivor Diet" of naturally gluten-free rice replacing the gluten-containing wheat that is a major staple of the Western diet being the treatment for it. Though also a bit of a Zig-Zagged example as, by her own admission, there was a period in the Outback when she feltbetterthan she had in a long time, with chronic stomach problems she suffered from disappearing during the game. It was this fact (and the return of her symptoms after her boot,) that helped her and her doctors determine she was suffering from an undiagnosed case of Celiac Disease, and the "Survivor Diet" of naturally gluten-free rice replacing the gluten-containing wheat that is a major staple of the Western diet being the treatment for it. Everyone Loves Blondes: Just about the entire tribe likes her. The Ingenue: Elisabeth was the first recurrence of the SurvivorIngénuearchetype, of which Colleen Haskell was the prototype. Elisabeth was portrayed as a very sweet and innocent girl. Rodger referred to her as a daughter figure to him. Alicia also referred to Elisabeth as "meek and mild". Intergenerational Friendship: With Rodger.

characters.name: Rodger Bingham
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Kentucky Joe Cool Old Guy: A generally calming presence on the show, develops a cute friendship with Elisabeth and is respected enough to outlast other Ogakor members. Face Your Fears: Rodger is afraid of heights AND just learned how to swim right before he came to the Outback. But he still jumps off a large waterfall for one of the earlier challenges. Heroic Sacrifice: Actually requests to go out fifth so Elisabeth Filarski-Hasselbeck can make the final four. Intergenerational Friendship: With Elisabeth. When he gave her a heart-shaped rock to give to her boyfriend.

characters.name: Amber Brkich
characters.description: After All-Stars, Amber competed with Rob on seasons7and11ofThe Amazing Race. Amber later competed onWinners at War. Born Lucky: Amber said she was lucky to be in an alliance with Boston Rob and to not be voted out at Final Tribal Council. Catchphrase: Surprisingly averted. Not once in this season does she say her old catchphrase of "Oh my god, it's so good!"Mario from Funny 115 even wrote about it in his website, here is the paragraph,"Do you even have to ask if I went through All-Stars and counted the number of times Amber says "Oh my godddd, it's sooooo good"? Hell yeah, of course I did! But guess what? She never says it during All-Stars. Not even once. Amber must have watched Australia back in 2001 and gotten annoyed with herself too, because it's like she made a conscious effort not to say it at any point during All-Stars. And that superhuman ability to change and adapt is what made Lamber the single best player in Survivor history. Just admit it, she is now officially the best of the best." Mario from Funny 115 even wrote about it in his website, here is the paragraph, Dark Horse Victory: Didanyoneexpect Amber of all people to win going into the season?A paragraph from Mario Lanza's Funny 115 says about this,"By the way, nowadays Amber is mostly known as being Boston Rob's wife. She is also known as the winner of All-Star Survivor. She beat the All-Stars, she was the best of the best, and by definition that means she is now the single best player in the history of Survivor. Isn't that depressing? Little Lamber is officially the best player in the history of Survivor. And it's true. Oh my godddddd. It's soooooooo true."

characters.name: Nick Brown
characters.description: The Lancer: To Kucha. Lazy Bum: Subverted. He was edited this way, but by all accounts from fellow cast members, this wasManipulative Editing. Out of Focus: He had the least content of any contestant on the season. The Stoic: By far the least emotional player on this season. Even when one of his Kucha tribemates ends up badly burned, his reaction is far more understated than anyone else's. Worthy Opponent: To Colby. Aside from Keith, he was the only real competition to him in the individual challenges.

characters.name: Jerri Manthey
characters.description: Jerri was chosen to compete onAll-Starsand laterHeroes Vs. Villains. Affably Evil: She's pretty nice in person. And There Was Much Rejoicing: Her castaways really disliked her attitude and were glad to be rid of her. Bitter Sweet Ending: Jerri became the most hated woman in America at the end ofSurvivor, saying that her return was one of the loneliest experiences for her. However, she was a struggling actress working at a bar for the past decade and she notes that her appointment book filled up after her appearance. Breakout Character: Ends up appearing in two seasons among a cast of legends.

characters.name: Alicia Calaway
characters.description: Amazonian Beauty: Alicia was a fitness trainer. Exact Words: While casting her vote for Amber (to win) at the Final Tribal Council, she smugly reminds Boston Rob of her promise to "never write [his] name down" and says that she is a woman of her word. Giving Someone the Pointer Finger: In her Jury Speech, much to the delight of theDVD Commentary. My Greatest Second Chance: She lasted slightly longer this time than inAustralian Outback. History Repeats: Once again, Alicia gave her jury vote to a woman who would win over an man at Final Tribal Council in a 4-3 vote.

characters.name: Jeff Varner
characters.description: Varner was chosen via public vote to return forCambodia, and would later return forGame Changers. Jerk with a Heart of Gold:Lovedstirring the pot and antagonizing people. He was actually the catalyst for Alicia and Kimmi's argument over the chickens. The Smart Guy: To Kucha. Tall, Dark, and Snarky Too Dumb to Live: By volunteering to quit the first individual immunity challenge, Jeff left himself open to elimination at Tribal Council. This was what Ogakor were hoping for as they took advantage of his past votes to force a tie and get him eliminated.

characters.name: Michael Skupin
characters.description: Michael would later return forPhilippines. Crazy Survivalist: He seriously manages tocatch and kill a pig.The editors also had fun portraying him like this now and then with some judicious use of close-up shots and eerie music. Dead Star Walking: The early episodes build Michael up as the undisputed (well, other than Alicia)Large Hamleader of Kucha, with some viewers even seeing him as the second coming ofRichard Hatch. He's arguably the biggest character from the first half of this season other than Jerri. And he ends up falling into the fire a day or two before the merge. Fatal Flaw: Carelessness, in a case ofReal Life Writes the Plot. Michael was ridiculously nonchalant about getting cut up repeatedly in his first day at camp, but right before the merge, when the game was going to really get underway and he was very set to go far, his recklessness caught up with him and he got injured so badly that Michael had to be evacuated and have his injuries treated by medical professionals and undergo monitoring in a hospital. Foreshadowing: On hisvery first dayas a castaway, Michael gets himself cut and bruised over and over, including getting a gash on his forehead, a puncture in the sole of his foot, and several nicks and slices from mishandling a knife. Tribemates were disturbed and cringing at how many injuries he kept getting and hisbrazen dismissal of them. Even so, Michael manages to be a strong player up to the looming of the merge. Finally, Michael stumbled and fell into acamp fire, and suffered extreme burns to his hands that were life-threatening and incapable of being healed properly during the game and would prevent him from further participation.

characters.name: Kimmi Kappenberg
characters.description: Kimmi was chosen via a public vote to return forCambodia. Alliterative Name:KimmiKappenberg. Break the Cutie: After Mike caught and killed the pig, Jeff started to mock Kimmi for her vegetarianism. Later, Jeff instigated an argument between her and Alicia over when to cook the chickens. The latter argument is what contributed towards Kimmi getting voted off.Earlier than that, she refused to eat a cow brain because it went against her values. Earlier than that, she refused to eat a cow brain because it went against her values. Did Not Think This Through: Signing on to do Survivor as a staunch vegetarian. Did Kimmi not watch the first season, where contestants were so hungry that they literally caught and ate rats?

characters.name: Mitchell Olson
characters.description: Didn't See That Coming: The first true blindside of the season. He and Jerri thought their five-person alliance was solid and were shocked at Tina and Colby’s betrayal. Fire of Comfort: Mitchell personally wrote several songs that Ogakor members sang together around the fire every night. The Ogakor members were disappointed that none were shown on-air (though at least one sceneappears on the DVD). Hide Your Gays: His Sexuality was not discussed on the show and he was the fourth out. The Load: Considering he's taller than most of the cast, he needed way more food and nutrients than the rest of his tribe. As said by Tina when she votes him out:Tina:"This game isn't easy. I didn't come out here to starve myself and face the elements to keep the weakest person." One Head Taller: Than the entire cast - he'sseven foot.

characters.name: Maralyn Hershey
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: The oldest woman on the cast. Genki Girl: Believe it or not, Maralyn is an older version of this. Intergenerational Friendship: With Amber, who was her "Mad Pup". I Was Quite a Looker: As revealed at theReunion. The Load: The reason she was voted out was because of her lack of athleticism.

characters.name: Kel Gleason
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: Jerri was this to him. On the post-show "Back From The Outback" special, he even had aDartboard of Hatewith her face on it. The Big Guy: Kel was physically bigger than evenColbyand was a former Army Ranger. Yet, he was stillthe first person from his tribe voted out. Fish Out of Water: Like Debb below, he had trouble relating to people who weren't from the military. Noodle Incident: The infamous "Beef Jerky Incident" (the question of whether or not he smuggled food into the game) has never been answered, and we never actually saw the footage of Kel chewing on whatever it was that he was chewing on (he claims it was a shard of grass).According to Jeff Varner'sAMAfrom Reddit, he did. Jeff reveals that Kel was caught in front of all the contestants by airport customs for trying to smuggle beef jerky, even having a seam on his pants for it. And later he was caught again for smuggling shoes on game day. According to Jeff Varner'sAMAfrom Reddit, he did. Jeff reveals that Kel was caught in front of all the contestants by airport customs for trying to smuggle beef jerky, even having a seam on his pants for it. And later he was caught again for smuggling shoes on game day.

characters.name: Debb Eaton
characters.description: Fish Out of Water: Had trouble relating to her tribe, leading to them ousting her first. Humiliation Conga: Not on the show itself, but as revealed on the post-show "Back From The Outback", the prisoners in the prison that she works at have been subjecting her to this by continuously mocking her for being the first person voted off of Survivor. It's pretty hard not to feel sorry for her after hearing about this. Small Role, Big Impact: She was voted off first, but the one vote she cast (against Jeff) ended up being the tiebreaker vote that gave Ogakor the upper hand at the merge, eventually leading to the elimination of the entire Kucha tribe and Tina's victory. Attentive viewers may notice that Kimmi did also vote for Jeff in the episode where she was voted off, it just wasn't tallied in front of the group due to Kimmi receiving the majority of votes before it came up. Even if Debb hadn't voted for Jeff, he still would have had more votes than Colby and been eliminated. Tomboy: A prison guard, and a particularly intimidating one at that.

characters.name: Samburu
characters.description: A House Divided: Compared to Boran, who was super chill the entire time, Samburu was pretty much a trainwreck the entire time. Divided We Fall: The separation between generations came to bite them hard in the long run. Dwindling Party: They were 4-6 come to the merge, and by the final four, no original Samburu members were left. Law of Chromatic Superiority: Subverted. While the red colored Samburu would win the first two immunity challenges and all but two of the reward challenges, Samburu would struggle internally as the game went on, losing half of their members by the merge as a majority alliance in Boran would dominate the individual game and take out Samburu until none were left at the final four. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: The tribe was split between old and young.

characters.name: Boran
characters.description: The Ace: Not initially, but after voting out Diane and Jessie, Boran performed better in the challenges and set themselves in a favorable position come the merge thanks to the tribe swap. Four-Philosophy Ensemble: The final four.Ethan = The Optimist.Kim J. = The Apathetic.Lex = The Cynic.Big Tom = The Realist. Ethan = The Optimist. Kim J. = The Apathetic. Big Tom = The Realist.

characters.name: Moto Maji
characters.description: The merged tribe of the season. Curb-Stomp Battle: The Samburu tribe's infighting came to a head at the merge, which put the more cohesive Boran in a de facto alliance. Accordingly, the final four all began at Boran, with the final two having never left it until the merge. Fire/Water Juxtaposition: The tribe name Moto Maiji is a combination of two Swahili words for fire (Moto) and water (Maiji).

characters.name: Ethan Zohn
characters.description: Ethan returned forAll-Stars,Winners at War, and competed onThe Amazing Race 19withJenna Morasca. Actually Pretty Funny: Ethan clearly found Tom's infamous "HE'S A JEW!" moment more funny than offensive given that he spends that moment doubled over in laughter. Afro Asskicker: His most notable physical characteristic. Always Second Best: Obviously averted in the end but Ethan often fell just short of winning challenges due to Lex's immunity run, to a point where Ethan openly told the cameras how tired he was of his own friend winning. Blue Is Heroic: Always wears a blue shirt which happens to be the most vibrantly colored shirt on the show

characters.name: "Big" Kim Johnson
characters.description: Chekhov's Gun: Kim's luxury item was a set of acrylic paints. They would be used in the SOS Challenge, giving Boron their first immunity win. Cool Old Lady: Kim was the oldest person by Birthdate to make it to the final tribal council.noteKim was the oldest person, in general, to make it to Day 39 and Final Tribal Council untilBob Crowleymade it to the end at 57 years old while Kim was 56 at the time of filming. Cool Teacher: Her job before retiring. Down to the Last Play: The only reason Tom and Lex were the fourth and third placers was that she somehow won two clutch immunities. Graceful Loser: She picks Ethan because she would lose no matter what.

characters.name: Alexis "Lex" van den Berghe
characters.description: Anti-Hero: As part of the original Mogo Mogo alliance. The Chessmaster: On Mogo-Mogo at least. Deal with the Devil: And, boy, did it end badly. Death Glare: His basic expression while he was on the jury. Digging Himself Deeper: During the reunion, when he tried to justify why he can get away with playing ruthlessly, but Rob can't, especially after Richardcalled him out on his hypocrisy.And later when he claimed that the necklace scene (seeOh, Crap!below) was manipulative editing. One can use one's eyes to see that it isn't, as Big Tom's shadow is visible getting up to vote.(See here)◊

characters.name: "Big" Tom Buchanan
characters.description: Big Tom returned forAll-Stars. Big Fun: The funniest person of the season. The Big Guy: It's in the nickname, after all. Fans have commented on him being even bigger in person. Can't Take Criticism: Though he was always going to vote for Ethan, his diatribe towards Kim reeks of this. She had previously said that he was sexist and that she didn't learn anything from him and he got really mad, despite not showing any animosity previously. Cool Old Guy: Among the oldest people in the game, and a textbook example ofBig Fun.

characters.name: Teresa "T-Bird" Cooper
characters.description: Teresa was a candidate forCambodia: Second Chancebut failed to get enough votes to return. Beneath Suspicion: She had a clear motive for voting for Lex (voting for Clarence would have been dishonorable), but no one connects the dots that she might have done it because she's so sweet and trustworthy. Cassandra Truth: She brings up the idea of voting Ethan out, knowing that his kindness and physical prowess would probably grant him the victory. She's ignored and Ethan ends up winning. Deus ex Machina: The first-ever tribe switch. It doesn't let her win the game, but she goes a hell of a lot further than if she were still in the Samburu tribe. She managed to outlast the Mall Rats after they did their best to pick them off. Last of Their Kind: She's the final Samburu member by the final five after Kim P is voted out.

characters.name: Kimberly "Little Kim" Powers
characters.description: The Cutie: Attempts to fill the role thatColleen HaskellandElisabeth Filarskidid before her. Et Tu, Brute?: Kim was shocked that Brandon flipped on Samburu. Girly Girl: To her Samburu "Mall Rat" alliance. Male Gaze: Not usually, but we get a lot of shots of her butt when the tribe showers together. Ms. Fanservice: Considered the "hot chick" of the season.

characters.name: Frank(lin) Garrison
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: He's anti-social and a little rough around the edges, and in a social game likeSurvivor, you do not want to be this. The Comically Serious: Occasionally filled this role. For example, in a game of I Never, the raunchiest thing he could think of was dishonoring a handshake. Crazy Survivalist: In one episode he said that if he weren't playing the game for his friends or family, he would dump all the water and food that wasn't his own so the younger, brattier members of his tribe would suffer. Also, in one interview post-show, he said he regretted that he wasn't able to hunt on the national preserve they were stranded in. Deadpan Snarker: Anytime somebody criticized him or he perceived somebody as criticizing him:Carl: Hey Frank, what branch of the service were you in?"Frank: I was in the American branch. It's calledfreedom. Deus ex Machina: Though all it accomplished was letting him reach the jury stage, he would have been the next on Samburu's hit list had the tribe swap not happened.

characters.name: Brandon Quinton
characters.description: Be Careful What You Wish For: In his boot episode, Brandon said he rather be voted next than being in an alliance with Frank. Guess What happened. Camp Gay: To be fair about it though, Brandon wasn't weak in the challenges and stood up for himself. His personality though was as gay as a three-dollar bill. False Friend: In the episode after Lindsey’s vote-off (where she became very emotional and said she was happy she hasn’t betrayed her “friend” Brandon), Brandon drags her name through the mud in a confessional, deriding her for being whiny and saying he’s glad he doesn’t have to deal with her anymore. Hilarity Ensues: When Brandon and Frank won an obstacle course reward challenge and got to see the movieOut of Africatogether at a drive-in. Honor Before Reason: one of the reasons he tanked his game was because he hated Frank's beliefs and refused to continue working with him.

characters.name: Kelly Goldsmith
characters.description: Anti-Villain: Only flipped because of Lex targeting her because he wrongfully believed that Kelly voted against him. The Cassandra: She was the first one to point out Lex's massive ego and hypocrisywhen it comes to him voting out friends and allies at the drop of a hat but freaking out when he gets even ''one'' vote cast against him. No one listened to her, though nobody in that season really got it in the same way she did. Death by Pragmatism: When she realizes that she was getting the boot, Kelly did the only sensible thing and flipped to Samburu. However, Brandon's flip still gotten her voted out. The Heart: To her Boran tribe. Jerkass: She doesn't always show it, but it came up at times such as her final tribal council speech and saying Frank should be put on medication to cure his introversion.

characters.name: Clarence Black
characters.description: The Atoner: By the time he got voted out in 10th, he'd more than redeemed himself for his earlier transgressions regarding his appetite. Being Good Sucks: Decides to feed Diane because she wasn't feeling good and it bites him in the ass, placing him at the bottom of the totem pole when the merge happened. Big Eater: Half of Clarence's story arc revolved around him being hungry all the time and eating food whenever he could get his hands on it. The Big Guy: The reason why he wasn't voted out after eating the Beans is that he was capable in challenges unlike Diane and later Jessie. You Lose at Zero Trust: Subverted. A pretty big deal was made over him eating extra cherries and a can of beans. Normally, that would be cause enough to kick most people out but he was a physical asset. When his time came, he'd made up for his mistakes and they acknowledged that he'd grown as a person. He wasn't kicked out because they couldn't trust him, but because he was a physical threat.

characters.name: Lindsey Richter
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: Was very condescending towards the older tribe after Carl's vote-off and she often liked to brag about being up for anything. She got better, though. Chekhov's Boomerang: The votes against her in her first Tribal Council, with Silas use it to keep the other tribe members safe and with her friends trying to protect her. Know When to Fold 'Em: The moment she and Tom were tied, she started saying her goodbyes before the revote, knowing she already had four against her. Lady Macbeth: As Silas rose to power, she became his right-hand woman and her cruelty towards the older Samburu rose to a head. Ms. Fanservice: She’s quite pretty. Even a nasty scrape she receives on her cheek mostly just accentuates it.

characters.name: Silas Gaither
characters.description: Arc Villain: Of the first half of the season. Asshole Victim: Fell victim to a major twist, had his entire new tribe pretty much conspire to take him out by all but throwing an immunity challenge to get rid of him, and since it wasSilasthere wasn't exactly a huge uproar from the fanbase. Backstab Backfire: See below in Cosmic Plaything. Cosmic Plaything: In what is perhaps the ultimate example ofHoist by His Own PetardinSurvivor, Silas was the first victim of the tribal swap, a twist he never could have predicted. What's worse was that the swap took place only a week after he betrayed the people he initially aligned with so he could be the leader of Samburu, and the people he got stuck with were the very people he betrayed! Diabolus ex Machina: He was a dominant leader of Samburu until he became the first-ever victim of the tribe swap. He had no way of trying to rectify his situation. Granted, he did put himself in that situation.

characters.name: Linda Spencer
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: Silas and the younger people noted a split in their tribe and the older people were getting picked off. He wanted to direct all of the older tribe's votes towards Lindsay to use her as a scapegoat until she asked "What's in it for us?" The older tribe members then voted him so that he'd be in a precarious position in case he ever had a tie vote against him. Cloud Cuckoolander: The younger tribe noted that she had two sides to her. One was a kindly mother figure, the other was a crazy woman. The latter facet often surfaced. Defiant to the End: She and the rest of the old people were on the chopping block and Silas wanted them to follow his instructions to keep the rest of the tribe safe. They refused to do that because he was an asshole and, on her boot episode, wrote down his name despite him being completely safe. Holier than Thou: Averted, although she did often bring up her belief that the gods were invoking bad luck on her tribe for its disharmony. Inspirationally Disadvantaged: According to herBioLinda beat out cancer.

characters.name: Carl Bilancione
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Carl was the oldest person on Samburu. Grumpy Old Man: Complained that the Gen X-ers on his tribe were behaving frivolously and not dependable. Ironically, this would be the same argument brought up by that aging generation inMillennials vs. Gen X. Laser-Guided Karma: It was noted that he had a Mercedes and a Porsche, and didn't need the money due to his career and doctorate status. He tried to push for the younger people to go due to not seeing fellowship in them, which helped fracture Samburu into the youths versus senority. Then, Carl was eliminated after a deadlocked vote against Lindsey in a sudden death African trivia tiebreaker when he missed a question that she got right. Sacrificial Lamb: His elimination started a chain of events that divided the Samburu tribe and that pretty much handed the loyalty of Frank and T-Bird to Boran.

characters.name: Yesenia "Jessie" Camacho
characters.description: Action Girl: She's a cop inReal Life. Dead Star Walking: Jessie had one of the highest pre-show scores in the popularity poll on CBS.com, and was one of the players the commercials focused on most. Needless to say, her popularity dropped dramatically after the first episode showed her being sick and unable to actively compete in challenges and plot strategy back at camp. Token Minority: The first latin castaway in the series.

characters.name: Diane Ogden
characters.description: Backstab Backfire: Lied about sharing a can of beans with Clarence to make it look like he was the only one at fault for using rations up too fast, when he did that because Diane was sick. Boran did grill Clarence in Tribal Council, but chose to spread most of their votes onto Diane because she was the one in poorer condition and potentially more burdensome. We Hardly Knew Ye: She was the first to be voted out of the game.

characters.name: Rotu
characters.description: Badass Crew: Before Koror, Rotu was the most dominant tribe to have existed in Survivor. Team Spirit: At least untilRob, Sean, and Vecepiashowed up.

characters.name: Maraamu
characters.description: Divided We Fall: Because there were separate alliances in Maraamu, there was very little harmony inside the tribe, which led to members being voted out one by one. Dwindling Party: Before we hadUlongas our officialFailure Tribe, we hadMaraamu. Epic Fail: Before Ulong came around, Maraamu was considered as the worst tribe due to losing all butthreechallenges (one of them being theironlyimmunity challenge), and had three members make it to the merge. Humiliation Conga: They only won ONE Immunity challenge. ONE. WITH ONE ORIGINAL MEMBER OF THE TRIBE LEFT! Slobs Versus Snobs: Rob, Sean, Vecepia, Sarah (slobs) vs Hunter, Patricia, and Gina (snobs).

characters.name: Soliantu
characters.description: As Long as It Sounds Foreign: Their name. The "sol" part does mean "sun" in Latin, but the rest is absolutely made-up.

characters.name: Vecepia "Vee" Towery
characters.description: Breaking Old Trends: When an alliance is down 7-2 they usually lose, same with being down 1-4. Vecepia's survival is incredibly notable for beating these odds alone. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Betrayed Kathy at the final three immunity challenge by making a deal with Neleh (right in front of Kathy even!) and letting her take it, which at the time was one of the most underhanded and despised moves the game had ever seen. Dark Horse Victory: The first person to win the game when their tribe entered the merge in the minority. Face–Heel Revolving Door: Depends on who the narrator is, but is also accompanied by her constant flips. She was with Hunter's alliance until the rowdy upstarts kicked him off. Then she distanced herself from the underdog Maaramus in the hopes that they'd leave before she did. She teams up with Sean, who becomes the season's hero after John's elimination, before going heel and betraying Kathy during the FTC. Guile Heroine: The very first under the radar winner.

characters.name: Neleh Dennis
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Basically what Sean accused her of being. Digging Yourself Deeper: Was completely incapable of answering jury questions at the Final Tribal Council in a way that didn't sound like pandering to the jury, which led to 3/4ths of the Rotu alliance voting for Vecepia (who was fully willing to admit that she played the game and had a strategy from day one).The chewed mint scene, she offers a chewed mint to the other tribemates after a reward trip with Paschal. While her intentions are pure and sweet, it felt insulting and condescending to the other tribemates. The chewed mint scene, she offers a chewed mint to the other tribemates after a reward trip with Paschal. While her intentions are pure and sweet, it felt insulting and condescending to the other tribemates. Gosh Darn It to Heck!: "Oh my Heck". Hypocrite: Basically how her actions came off to the jury, condemning them for lying and forming alliances while doing the same thing.

characters.name: Kathleen "Kathy" Vavrick-O'Brien
characters.description: The Cassandra: Sees exactly how the Chapera alliance is going to play out once she and Shii-Ann were gone and tries to get the people who were inevitably going to get voted out to do something about it. They didn't. Crazy-Prepared: Before All Stars started, Kathy went to a psychologist to have them analyze some of the personality profiles of people she thought might be picked for this season in order to determine which players would be easiest to manipulate, hardest to trust, best to form an alliance with, etc. Determinator: How she won the first individual immunity challenge. Graceful Loser:Zig-Zagged. She did vote for Boston Rob, who hurt her more. However, she liked him and disliked Amber for building on that final 6 deal Boston Rob offered to Lex. Or maybe she just preferred Rob because she liked him to begin with. Irony: In her last voting confessional before being voted out, Kathy said that Amber had no chance of winning without changing her her game. Guess who won?

characters.name: Paschal English
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Highly respected among his peers. He was still able to win a challenge. Diabolus ex Machina: Arguably had the best chance of winning but was screwed by the purple rock. Dirty Old Man: He says that he's in heaven being the lone man among three women. However, his scandals involving younger women may make his relationship with Neleh suspect. Face–Heel Turn: The thirteenth episode had him and Neleh throw Sean and V under the bus for something they didn't even do. Four Is Death: The fourth placer in this fourth installment, and was eliminated most controversially ever.

characters.name: Sean Rector
characters.description: Badass Boast: As he made his vote against John and kicked off the downfall of the Rotu alliance:"Checkmate, bro. Thought you had me. Tell you any time you go to Vegas, bet on black." Badass Teacher: Not only has he won a teacher of the year award, but he's also one of the biggest challenge threats of the season. Be Yourself: Stated this in the 8th episode. Cool Teacher: InReal Life. Dragon Ascendant: Closely aligned with Boston Rob right up until his elimination, after which he had a big hand in forming the five-person alliance with V, Kathy, Paschal, and Neleh to oust the Rotu 4.

characters.name: Robert "The General"DeCanio
characters.description: Bad Liar: After John's demise, he attempts to distance himself from the group by saying that he never gave his word and that he was going through the motions. Aside from the fact that the new five alliance doesn't buy it, theaudienceknows for a fact that what he's saying is not true. The Big Guy: To the Rotu alliance. Last of His Kind: Ends up being the longest-lasting member of the Rotu 4 Alliance, as John was targeted first due to being the group's leader, Zoe was next as a clear threatfor her shiftinessand relative challenge strength, and Tammy was taken out because she was the only viable candidate left when Robert won individual immunity for himself. Made of Iron: Robert cut his toe with John had to cut the injured pieces of. Despite the pain, Robert said you had to deal with it. It's pretty much a non-issue after the episode it was introduced. Non-Indicative Name: "The General" refers to one of his tattoos, which you can see on his right shoulder in his photo. He was never involved with any military, nor was he an attorney general or surgeon general.

characters.name: Tamara "Tammy" Leitner
characters.description: Action Girl: She won two consecutive immunity challenges. Determinator: Tammy stated she isn't giving up unless her name is called out at tribal council. The Rotu 4 down to the Rotu 2, she was fighting a losing battle and kept on fighting. The Lancer: Of the Rotu alliance. She was often referred to as a "pitbull" because of this. "The Reason You Suck" Speech: Just likeSusanandKelly Goldsmithshe opts to rant about everything she hates about the final two. Lampshaded during the reunion show by Rosie O'Donnell, who remarked that she was giving Tammy the "Sue Hawk Award".

characters.name: Zoe Zanidakis
characters.description: Backstab Backfire: Attempted to ditch the Rotu alliance once John was voted out, and claimed she was never loyal to them. She still got voted out next. Bad Liar: A few times after the switch. One example is when Kathy asks her if she's going to vote Kathy out, Zoe pauses for over ten seconds. Then she says no. Oops. The Big Girl: Or as Rob says, "the toughest guy on the tribe." Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: After John's elimination, Zoe declared she never liked Tammy. Graceful Loser: The only member of the Rotu alliance willing to admit that Neleh could beat her. As a result, she's also the only member to vote for Neleh to win.

characters.name: John Carroll
characters.description: Ascended Fanboy: He applied three times to get casted(ever sinceSeason ''One''), and this is the lucky time he made it on. Big Bad Wannabe: Establishes a pecking order based on what he believed to be the blind allegiance of the original Rotu members, who severely outnumbered Sean and Vecepia once the merge hit. Drunk with Power: What happens after the Gabriel blindside. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: He found it so hard to believe that Gabriel genuinely wasn't interested in cutthroat strategy that it put him into a paranoid spiral that culminated in voting Gabriel out. Fatal Flaw: Pride. His overconfidence that everybody is willing to bow down to him to the point of outright gloating is what convinces Paschal and Neleh to flip.

characters.name: "Boston" Rob Mariano
characters.description: After All-Stars, Rob competed with Amber on seasons7and11ofThe Amazing Race. Rob later competed onHeroes vs. Villains,Redemption Island, andWinners at War. He also served as a mentor onIsland of the Idols. The Ace: He won four out of the seven individual immunity challenges during the merge, two rewards, and was basically the one who carried Chapera in challenges during the pre-merge. Plus he used his construction experience to help build the best shelter of all three tribes. Bittersweet Ending: He lost the game, but won a wife. Plus, it was his reputation from this appearance that let him compete twice more. Breakout Character: While he was already this inMarquesas, his performance this season is what elevated him to a Survivor legend. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Just askLex, Alicia, "Big" Tom, and Rob Cesternino.

characters.name: Gina Crews
characters.description: American Accents: She has a thick hearty southern one. Born Unlucky: Gina was stuck on Maraamu for all of her time in the game, having lost so many challenges in a row. Intergenerational Friendship: With Kathy after the tribe switch. Narrator: Has the highest average confessionals per episode. Only Sane Man: Gina saw herself like this when her tribe Maraamu voted out Hunter.

characters.name: Gabriel Cade
characters.description: Break the Cutie: His face tells a story of heartbreak and despair the moment he receives a unanimous vote. He cries during his final words and tells his tribe he still loves them. Diabolus ex Machina: The Tribe Switch brought the three people who brought the game with them.Even moreso, instead of booting those three people, his alliance voted for him for very little reason. Even moreso, instead of booting those three people, his alliance voted for him for very little reason. Digging Yourself Deeper: When asked about what his game plan was, Gabe said he wasn't there to play the game. This would start the events towards his elimination. Everyone Loves Blondes: A male variant. Reportedly, the staff and crew cried after his elimination.Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold

characters.name: Sarah Jones
characters.description: Diabolus ex Machina: The Tribe Switch. Sarah was separated from her alliance and was trapped with Gina (Sarah's biggest critic). The other people liked Sarah but not her lack of work ethic. Basically, she was screwed when Maraamu lost immunity. Establishing Character Moment: Her Cleopatra-like posing on the raft and her refusal to help row as her tribe made its way to camp on the first day. Four Is Death: The fourth person voted out in the fourth episode in the fourth season. When voted out, the vote was 4-1 and she was the fourth Maraamu to leave the game. The Load: Because of being aLazy Bumand Hunter thought she was distracting Rob. Even on the new Maraamu tribe, she didn't spend much time with the new members, leading to her getting eliminated. Ms. Fanservice: Sarah was the first woman to explicitly fill out this role.

characters.name: Hunter Ellis
characters.description: The Ace: The physically strongest and most capable member of his tribe.Ace Pilot: He was a former Navy Pilot. Ace Pilot: He was a former Navy Pilot. Decoy Protagonist: All-American, blonde guy with a great body and is liked by damn near everyone. Along with a lot of confessionals, the guy could have been this season'sColby. Rob, however, put a quick stop to that. Hero of Another Story: In later years, Hunter Ellis appeared in several actiony ads for Atomic products like the Atomic Beam Flashlight, Atomic Lantern, Atomic Headlight and Atomic Lighter. Intergenerational Friendship: With Patricia

characters.name: Patricia Jackson
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: The oldest woman in the game. Happily Married:Stated in her CBS Profile Intergenerational Friendship: With Hunter. The Load: Why she was targeted. Unlike manySurvivorexamples, she escapes the first My Beloved Smother: After she survives the first vote, she becomes this to her entire tribe!

characters.name: Peter Harkey
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoo Lander: And how! Hidden Depths: HisSurvivorOzinterview is a force to behold, and it gives a lot of depth and humanity to "that one guy who talked about his holes." Hoist by His Own Petard: Openly put a target on Patricia's back when Maraamu lost the first challenge, before anyone even bothered pointing fingers. This immediately turned everyone against him, and caused him to leave first. Intergenerational Friendship: With Sean Rector. Also formed one with Boston Rob after the game.

characters.name: Sook Jai
characters.description: A House Divided: First Jed, Robb, and Stephanie were immediately odds for seeming laziness and immaturity. The tribe threw at least one challenge just to get rid of them. Next, the remaining members managed to find new conflicts despite clear outcasts being gone. Lastly, the fake merge some of them try to associate with the Chuay Gahns, who ultimately couldn't save them. It cost each one of them their position in the game. Dwindling Party: It started with the fake merge, and it only got worse when only three members made it to the real merge. Failure Hero: How they ended up. Five-Man Band: The core members worked like this: Jake Billingsley; who assembled and led them. He was also the last one sent home. Penny Ramsey; the general informant for the group. Shii Ann Huang; the closest thing Sook Jai had to a strategist. Ken Stafford; the muscle whenever Jake was not enough. He was also more down-to-earth and skilled at mediation. Erin Collins, who tried to avoid drama at all cost and was close to Penny and Jake. Purple Is Powerful: Subverted. They started strong but ultimately lost challenges near the merge. This cost them the numbers advantage and they were pagonged.

characters.name: Chuay Gahn
characters.description: The Ace: They got pretty lucky winning more immunity challenges, even if they lost a good number of rewards. The Bad Guy Wins: Handily took down the Sook Jai in the end. Gray-and-Gray Morality: Instantly portrayed at the villains, but not to an even degree. Horrible Judge of Character: They never come close to figuring out Brian can't be trusted.

characters.name: Chuay Jai
characters.description: Curb-Stomp Battle: Within the tribe, the remainders of Sook Jai were dispatched almost immediately. The true drama was ultimately between the remnants of Chuay Gahn. Also, Brian Heidik didn't exactly have a hard time winning this season.

characters.name: Brian Heidik
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: Cannot remember Shii Ann's name and calls her "Soo-Yin" and "Sin-Jo" in the same sentence. This especially glaring when A) Ted had just said right before he started talking, and 2) he was an absolute control freak who was treating her favor as the most important thing. The Ace: He is the first winner of the final immunity challenge to win the game, as well as the first winner to also win the most individual immunity challenges in a season. Affably Evil: Nice to his tribemates and off the show, but absolutely has no qualms with backstabbing them. Badass Boast: The infamous "Mr. Freeze" confessional on how has teammates could not read the real him. He wasn't wrong. The Bad Guy Wins: Granted, for a medium-limited definition "bad guy".

characters.name: Clay Jordan III
characters.description: Fatal Flaw: He tends to lash out at people when they aggravate him. He did just that to Jake (the one Sook Jai thatdidn'tvote for him) at the jury questioning. Fetish: He has a thing for asses. Grumpy Old Man: Bordering on misanthropy. Jerkass: Almost certainly brought to the final two by Brian because nobody liked Clay or thought he deserved the million in the slightest.Jerk with a Heart of Gold: On the other hand, Clay took an active interest in all of the ex-Sook Jai members when the two tribes merged, unlikeBrian. While this was undoubtedly only due to strategy (all three of the votes he received to win during the Final Tribal Council came from ex-Sook Jais), at least he tried to know who each of them was. When it came to the Final Jury questioning, while neither came off well, Clay at the very least was able to pass Penny's "what do you know about me" question with flying colors whereas Brian failed in a completely embarrassing fashion. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: On the other hand, Clay took an active interest in all of the ex-Sook Jai members when the two tribes merged, unlikeBrian. While this was undoubtedly only due to strategy (all three of the votes he received to win during the Final Tribal Council came from ex-Sook Jais), at least he tried to know who each of them was. When it came to the Final Jury questioning, while neither came off well, Clay at the very least was able to pass Penny's "what do you know about me" question with flying colors whereas Brian failed in a completely embarrassing fashion.

characters.name: Jan Gentry
characters.description: Lady Drunk: As well as Jan herself, her friends and family who couldn't attend the Reunion show were all seen at a pub celebrating her third-place finish.Jeff: Where else would they be? Manchild: Particularly her reaction to the bidding challenge ("see ya, wouldn' wanna be ya!"), as well as finding a dead baby bat on the beach. My Tribe Right or Wrong: Said she would sink or swim with her tribe in the fifth episode. The Pawn: All but referred to by Brian as one. Sanity Slippage: During the animal graveyard scenes, at least.

characters.name: Helen Glover
characters.description: Boring, but Practical: Clay called her this, with different phrasing ("personality of an encyclopedia"). Deadpan Snarker: With a huge emphasis on deadpan. And on snarker. Et Tu, Brute?: As well as happening to her, she quoted that in her speech against Brian at the Final Tribal Council. Happily Married: It was obvious in the episode her husband appeared. Only Sane Man: While she was the only relatively sane person in her alliance, her husband who won the loved one's visit (he got to hang out with Chuay Jai for twenty-four hours) was also one. He observes right away that Brian is the one who's really controlling the tribe, and he tries to convince Helen to listen to him and vote Brian out. She doesn't listen.

characters.name: "Big" Ted Rogers Jr.
characters.description: Bald Head of Toughness: Used a shaving kit for his head, not his face. The Big Guy: They call him "Big" Ted for a reason. Can't Hold His Liquor: While Big Ted says that he never drank alcohol before, the first time hedid, he became totallyplastered. Genius Bruiser: A computer programmer back home. Gentle Giant: You can see him getting a little misty-eyed during Chuay Gahn's first vote, and when his tribe was planning to cook one of the chickens after the merge, Ted couldn't handle it (since he saw the chickens as pets) and went further down the beach to exercise.

characters.name: Jake Billingsley
characters.description: Blatant Lies: In one episode he told stories about his life that would make evenCoach Wadeshake his head. Cool Old Guy: The oldest contestant of the season and voted the most popular of the season. Did I Just Say That Out Loud?: In one episode before Sook Jai went to Tribal Council (at this point there were only four Sook Jais left, and they all seemed pretty close to each other), Penny suggested that whoever the three that were left should all sleep together that night, and Jake suddenly blurts out "That sounds almost erotic". Either this comes off ashilariousor asSquickdepending on your point of view. In-Series Nickname: The Chuay Gahn members started calling him "Jake the Snake" post-merge because he attempted to findsomeway to keep in the game. Noodle Incident: We don't get to hear about the adventures that Jake has had over the years (in the episodes where he told stories about his life), but one of them apparently involves something happening in the middle of an airport.

characters.name: Penny Ramsey
characters.description: Backstab Backfire: See the Quisling below Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: According to many of her castmates, including Ken, Shii Ann, and most of Chuay Gahn. Gossipy Hen: According to certain members of Sook Jai. HypocriteTook great delight in whacking other players at the kneecaps. When it was her turn, as evidenced by the way she set down her torch to be snuffed, she was as far from aGraceful Loseras anyone could get. Jerkass: Her rivalry with Shii-Ann bordered on racism.

characters.name: Ken Stafford
characters.description: Big Brother Mentor: To Robb. In Episode 6, after a quarrel over a misunderstanding, Ken takes Robb under his wing and becomes this to him, teaching Robb how to better relate to his tribe. This calmed down the normally very unpredictable Robb into having an epiphany about himself and suddenly becoming much nicer to his tribemates. The Big Guy: Of Sook Jai. Standing 6'5", Ken is still one of the tallest people to play the game. Only Sane Man: Incredibly level-headed and logical, and not prone to the weirder quirks of basically anyone else left at that point. Out of Focus: Almost invisible until episode six and his quarrel with Robb. But he at least gets more screentime then on. Worthy Opponent: To Brian. Ken saw Brian for what he was and warned Jake not to trust the used car salesman. In turn, the night of the fake merge Brian took Ted aside and warned him to watch out for Ken. Once the tribes merged Ken was eliminated immediately, likely because he was by far the biggest threat to Brian's dominance.

characters.name: Erin Collins
characters.description: Ms. Fanservice: Defied. Erin chose to wear her shirt over her bikini top at all times specifically to avoid being this. Out of Focus: Tried her hardest to avoid the drama engulfing her tribe. Those Two Girls: With Penny

characters.name: Shii Ann Huang
characters.description: All of the Other Reindeer: Post-merge. Ascended Fangirl: Actually uses the term "Pagonged" on-camera to describe what happened to Mogo Mogo, and early on showed reluctance to vote out Richard Hatch "because he's the king" and it would be no fun to get rid of him early. Foreshadowing: In her Final words, she warns the others about Amber and how she slips through the cracks. Graceful Loser: One of theonlyones on the jury. Last of Her Kind: The last Mogo Mogo left.

characters.name: Robert "Robb" Zbacnik
characters.description: Boisterous Bruiser: Might not be the most helpful around camp, but will take any excuse to go apeshit in a challenge. Coming of Age Story: His final episode. Crying Wolf: SeeFunny Background Event Dumb Muscle: More "immature" muscle, but he's still the Sook Jai most likely to make a stupid decision.Dumbass Has a Point: The reason he took a skateboard to a beach was because his first two suggestions for luxury item had already been taken. When he was informed of this, he sarcastically asked "What am i supposed to bring, a skateboard?".The producers wound up giving him one for the trip. Dumbass Has a Point: The reason he took a skateboard to a beach was because his first two suggestions for luxury item had already been taken. When he was informed of this, he sarcastically asked "What am i supposed to bring, a skateboard?".The producers wound up giving him one for the trip.

characters.name: Stephanie Dill
characters.description: Girlish Pigtails: Wears these often Lazy Bum: Why she was alligned with Jed and Robb. Naked People Are Funny: In her audition video, she was naked. Out of Focus: Stephanie didn't do much during her time on the show because of her sickness.

characters.name: Ghandia Johnson
characters.description: Dude, Not Funny!: Her reaction to John's joke about Chuay Gahn's water source. Four Is Death: Fourth one out and had voted votes against her.

characters.name: Jed Hildebrand
characters.description: Lazy Bum: According to his tribe. Out of Focus: Not as badly as many examples, but definitely there. Granted part of this is... We Hardly Knew Ye: The first person in the "lesser screentime tribe" eliminated.

characters.name: Tanya Vance
characters.description: Disappeared Dad: He died shortly after Tanya left to compete on the show. The Ingenue: Tanya probably belongs to the SurvivorIngénuearchetype. She seemed to be cast for the innocent sweetheart role. Nice Girl: Well-liked by her tribe, voted out only because of her illness.

characters.name: John Raymond
characters.description: I Coulda Been a Contender!: At the Reunion, Jeff Probst comments on how John was probably the most well-prepared first boot ever (for surviving in the wild), and he says that on any other season John probably could have done much better. Pointy-Haired Boss: His tribe voted him off for being too bossy.

characters.name: Jaburu
characters.description: Amazon Brigade: Quite literally, given the season's setting. Animal Motif: Named after a stork.

characters.name: Tambaqui
characters.description: All Men Are Perverts: At least how they were edited as. Animal Motif: Named after a fish. Epic Fail: During the first immunity challenge, Daniel and Ryan had trouble with the balance beam after taking an early lead. Jaburu gained immunity and Ryan was voted out of Tambaqui as a result. Total Party Kill: None of the Day 14 iteration of Tambaqui made it to the Final Three.

characters.name: Jacaré
characters.description: Animal Motif: Named after a crocodile.

characters.name: Jenna Morasca
characters.description: Jenna would return to compete inAll-Stars. Action Girl: She won four out of the eight individual challenges during the merge. Jenna tiedKelly Wiglesworth's record for most individual immunity challenges by women in a single seasonnoteKim Spradlinalso tied this record. Anti Heroine: She's kind of bratty. Ascended Fangirl: Like Rob, Jenna has seen every season since the show began back in 2000. Batman Gambit: Giving her immunity (not the HII, but the individual immunity) to Heidi at the Final 6. She was banking on that Rob found her a jury goat.

characters.name: Matthew von Ertfelda
characters.description: Axe-Crazy: Many of the castaways thought he was this when he started sharpening the machete constantly. Batman Gambit: Threw the final challenge because heknewthat both Rob and Jenna would want to take him to the final two.Unfortunately for him, the reason they both wanted to take him is because theyknewhe was an easy finale opponent to beat. Unfortunately for him, the reason they both wanted to take him is because theyknewhe was an easy finale opponent to beat. The Big Guy/The Starscream: Depending on where you are in the season; he's either a free vote that Rob can use, or he's going behind Rob's back by cutting deals with the other players to ensure that he gets to the final two. Bilingual Bonus: Spoke Mandarin with Daniel in one episode.

characters.name: Rob Cesternino
characters.description: Rob would return to compete inAll-Stars. Ascended Fanboy: Probably the first overt fan of the show to make it on. There were other people in past seasons who were fans, but none to the degree that Rob was. The Chessmaster: His strategy for winning this season. *Cough* Snark *Cough*: After Butch accidentally burned down the camp. Deadpan Snarker: Had his moments, but not usually in mean spirit.

characters.name: Butch Lockley
characters.description: Be Yourself: His luxury item was a poster he got from the high school he is a principal at that said "BELIEVE IN YOURSELF". When the camp accidentally burned down, he exclaims "Well, now we'rereallygoing to have to believe in ourselves!". Happily Married: His family visit makes it clear that he and his wife are a cute couple. Older Sidekick: To Matthew, who was a key ally of. Pyromaniac: Rob called him one, presumably because he collected so much firewood. Said firewood was responsible for causing a huge fire back at camp while everyone was away at the reward challenge. Sanity Slippage: Was also accused of this late in the game.Hilarity Ensuestoo.

characters.name: Heidi Strobel
characters.description: Action Girl: Good enough in challenges to have that target on her back. Brainless Beauty: Varied wildly between this andFemme Fatale.Dumb Muscle: One of the stronger female contestants this season. Dumb Muscle: One of the stronger female contestants this season. Femme Fatale: On multiple occasions used her feminine wiles to get her way. But sometimes it's hard to tell when it's a fluke and when it'sObfuscating Stupidity. Hidden Depths: Has an IQ of 165.

characters.name: Christy Smith
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: Other players have said that Christy was... pretty out there, but the show mostly painted her as theInspirationally DisadvantagedNice Girlinstead and left out most of her wackiness. There are still hints of it in the show though, such as her story about having sex at the Washington Monument. Deadpan Snarker: Was often very sarcastic in confessionals. Drunk with Power: Why she was blindsided at the Final 6. Elmuh Fudd Syndwome: Because she's deaf, her way of speaking often tended to go like this. Hollywood Homely: Despite being a very attractive girl and the same age as Heidi she is never brought up in the same conversations as Jenna, Heidi and Shawna.

characters.name: Alex Bell
characters.description: Big Ol' Eyebrows: Sometimes they appear larger than his actual eyes. The Dulcinea Effect: Both supported and subverted. He was perfectly willing to betray all the men so he could align with Jenna, but during the pre-merge,hewas the one who convinced Shawna to forget about her alliance with Jenna, Heidi and Deena. Hoist by His Own Petard: He made it clear to Rob,right after they blindsided Deena, that he would be voted out at the final four. This was what caused Rob to make a counter-alliance of Matthew, Butch and Christy to vote Alex out. Older Than They Look: Alex acts in his twenties but was 33 at the time of filming.

characters.name: Deena Bennett
characters.description: Distaff Counterpart: To Roger. She was the unofficial leader of the women's tribe and seemed to not respect men.Manipulative Editingperhaps had a part to play. Hoist by Her Own Petard: Ironically goes out in a much similar way to Roger. She more or less threw her shot at immunity away not thinking she needed it, and it turned out she did. On an even more ironic note, the people who got rid of her were the very people that she thought she was manipulating into doing her bidding. Idiot Ball: Letting Matt win immunity even though she was a prime contender to go home next. Younger Than They Look: Even though she is only 2-3 years older than the youthful Alex, Deena is often referred to as one of the older contestants.

characters.name: Dave Johnson
characters.description: Always Someone Better: Why Alex and Rob wanted him gone. The Dulcinea Effect:After the tribal draft, he had the perfect opportunity to get rid of Jenna's best ally(Heidi) and fracture the women's tribe. For some bizarre reason, which can only be explained by this trope, he decided to spare Heidi and get rid ofBlack SheepJeanne instead.They were even on numbers 3/3 between him, Butch, and Roger and Jeanne, Christy and Heidi. For whatever reason, they perceived Heidi to be the easiest one to flip. After the tribal draft, he had the perfect opportunity to get rid of Jenna's best ally(Heidi) and fracture the women's tribe. For some bizarre reason, which can only be explained by this trope, he decided to spare Heidi and get rid ofBlack SheepJeanne instead. They were even on numbers 3/3 between him, Butch, and Roger and Jeanne, Christy and Heidi. For whatever reason, they perceived Heidi to be the easiest one to flip.

characters.name: Roger Sexton
characters.description: Fish Out of Water: To put it bluntly, Roger did not fit in with his much younger and hornier castmatesat all. This is best shown at the merge feast; while everyone else is happy to get drunk and have fun, Roger wants everyone to stop drinking and eating and start working on the shelter. Hated by All: Everyone was on board to make him the first boot of the merge and the episode didn't even try to hide it, even doubling up confessionals of everyone talking about how much they hated Roger.
