Pointy-Haired Boss: Was initially conceived as a target because he was bossy. Old Soldier: According to his pre-game bio, Roger served in theThe Vietnam War. Outliving One's Offspring: While not talked about in the show itself, Roger's daughter died in 1992 according to hispre-game bio.

characters.name: Shawna Mitchell
characters.description: Innocent Beta Bitch: In the Jaburu tribe'sGirl Posse, Jenna was theAlpha Bitch, Heidi wasThe Lancer(or if you will,The Dragon), and Shawna was this. Intergenerational Friendship: In herSurvivorOZ Interview, Shawna claims that Jeanne was her closest friend. Possibly reachingTrue Companions. Sanity Slippage: She had this when her tribe lost out on the Coke fridge. She got better. Suicide by Cop: Attempted but failed in the fourth episode. Instead, they kicked outJoAnna, and her indignance at this put her in genuine hot water. Tom Boy: Claims to be one in her Survivor Oz interview

characters.name: Jeanne Hebert
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: An early provider at camp, despite her age. Heterosexual Life-Partners: WithJoAnna. WhenJoAnnaleft, she was immediately the next target by association. Intergenerational Friendship: With Shawna. Her defense of Shawna wanting to be sent home wasn't just malice or strategy.

characters.name: JoAnnaWard
characters.description: The Fundamentalist: So religious in fact, that she considered the immunity idol an affront to the First Commandment "Thou Shalt Not Have Any Gods Before Me". Holier than Thou: She shows shades of this when she states that "Jesus loves Jaburu!". Insane Troll Logic: When Joanna compared the Immunity Idol to a religious idol(as in the First Commandment "Thou shalt not have any other gods before me.") Rob summed up most people's reactions to Joanna's reaction best when he waxed philosophic about whether God had any real vested interest inSurvivor. Religious Bruiser: She was one of the strongest members of the original Jaburu tribe. Shout-Out: When Ryan Howard fromThe Officename-dropped her in the middle of an episode. It came somewhat as a shock to some fans who would expect name drosp to more famous contestants like Rupert Boneham or Boston Rob. Someone working for The Office (US) was clearly a Survivor fan.

characters.name: Daniel Lue
characters.description: Asian and Nerdy: Somewhat averted, he seems to be pretty smart; but in terms ofSurvivorintelligence, he doesn't quite show similar results. He also knew fluent Mandarin and used it with tribemate Matthew von Ertfelda. Dumb Muscle: Portrayed as this, fairly or not. Limited Social Circle: After Ryan got voted out, Matthew became hisOnly Friend.

characters.name: Janet Koth
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: The oldest woman in the season's cast. The Load: The other reason why she was voted out. Mis-blamed: Mistaken for smuggling a granola bar into camp.

characters.name: Ryan Aiken
characters.description: Ironic Birthday: The episode he was voted out in aired on his birthday. Mis-blamed: In-universe example. He was blamed for blowing Tambaqui's lead in the first Immunity Challenge, but Daniel was the one who caused it to happen. Mr. Fanservice: Ryan is a model, after all. Shout-Out: References theJohn WoomovieHard Targetwhen voting for Roger by stating "Don't Hunt What You Can't Kill". Worthy Opponent: To Roger, both of whom were battling from Day 1 for control of the men's tribe.

characters.name: Drake
characters.description: A House Divided: Cracks slowly begin to form between Drake with a trio alliance of Rupert, Sandra, and Christa, and the single members such as Jon and Shawn. Freudian TrioSandra = Ego.Christa = Id.Rupert = Superego. Named After Somebody Famous: The Drake tribe is named after privateer Francis Drake, The Rival: To Morgan. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork

characters.name: Morgan
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Despite Savage making sure all the "alpha males" were kept around, they won very few challenges, and were somewhat screwed over by the outcast twist. Failure Hero: All of them (bar Skinny Ryan) were excellent in challenges, but failed to defeat the Drakes. Lil managed to take out their arch-enemy before losing, though. Named After Somebody Famous: The Morgan tribe is named after Henry Morgan. The Rival: To Drake, and especially to Fairplay. Team Spirit/Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: Depending on the situation.

characters.name: The Outcasts
characters.description: They won it, so both their former tribes had to send somebody home.The votes ultimately went to Lillian and Burton, who were originally voted out 3rd and 4th, but went on to far outstay many of their tribemates. My Greatest Second Chance: The gimmick of the tribe.

characters.name: Sandra Diaz-Twine
characters.description: Sandra would return toSurvivormultiple times, competing inHeroes Vs. Villains,Game Changers,Winners at War, and evenAustralian Survivor: Blood Vs. Wateralongside her daughter, Nina. She also appeared onIsland of the Idolsas a mentor. Anti Heroine: The kind of person who would not attempt to be coercive with people unless they rightfully deserved it. And this is before shelearned to quietly groom people to her advantage by acting nice and congenial just to lure them into a false sense of security and then manipulate them. Her record of success comes from the fact that she's very furtive and crafty, but learns to hide it well. Badass Boast: HerWham Linebelow was the first ever time Fairplay's "Dead Grandma" ploy failed to convince someone he was being truthful (which, of course, he wasn't). Her refusal to believe Jon and stick the woman's alliance together was the ultimate event that turned the game around for the three remaining women against Jon and Burton. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: With Rupert and Christa - she was Brains. Born Winner: Across her two winning seasons, she had only one vote counted against her (plus two negated by an idol inHeroes vs. Villains).

characters.name: Lillian "Lil" Morris
characters.description: Back From Elimination: Originally voted out 3rd, in what would have been 14th place. Being Good Sucks: She was constantly lambasted at the Final Tribal Council for her choice of wearing her scout master uniform. Of course, she didn't know she would be playing the game with it. Beware the Nice Ones: She may be aPerpetual Frownerand easily upset, but during the final immunity, she grows giant cannonballs ofsteel.She even taunts Jon as he tries to cut a deal with her. Cool Old Lady: The Oldest contestant this season. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: SeeShut Up, Hannibal!.Her uniform and her personality made most people write her off as being in over her head but after her return to the game she voted out the entire jury (and Savage), backstabbing several of them, and her social isolation meant she didn't have strong ties to any alliance and gave her considerable power in the game.

characters.name: Jon "Jonny Fairplay" Dalton
characters.description: Fairplay would later compete as a fan-favorite inMicronesia: Fans Vs. Favorites. And There Was Much Rejoicing: The two remaining women talk about how much they hated him after he's voted off. Big Bad: The most clearly defined villain Survivor ever had up to that point. Brains Evil, Brawn Good: Contrast him with the season's main hero, Rupert. Breakout Character: Still remembered as the most infamous villain to ever play untilRussell Hantzcame along.

characters.name: Darrah Johnson
characters.description: Action Girl: Won three Immunity Challenges in a row, finished fourth because nobody wanted to compete against her in the endurance challenge. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl Diabolus ex Machina: On her boot episode, the remaining four castaways had to compete against the Jury for immunity. As a result of the jury winning, she got the boot. Disqualification-Induced Victory: When she won her first immunity. Burton had his immunity stripped after Jeff discovered a misspelled word. Downplayed, since she still had to beat everyone else. Girly Girl: To Morgan.

characters.name: Burton Roberts
characters.description: Back from the Dead: Originally sent home 4th, in what would have been 13th place. Came Back Strong: Both from a gameplay and character standpoint, he becomes much more interesting and dominating upon coming back to take revenge on his old tribe. The Dog Bites Back: By being the main factor for why the Outcast Tribe beat both Drake and Morgan, he indirectly led to Shawn being voted out immediately after. He then proceeded to be a key factor in both Rupert and Christa being voted out. Demoted to Dragon: Initially the leader of one faction of Drake with his own dragon beingShawn, he ends up as Fairplay's dragon after returning. The Dragon: To Jon following his return, as mentioned above.

characters.name: Christa Hastie
characters.description: Action Girl: Lasted the longest out of her entire tribe in the 'hold a bar with weighted sandbags on it longer than anyone else' immunity challenge, and always came in extremely close to winning individual immunity (only loosing to Rupert or fellowAction GirlDarrah). Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: With Rupert and Sandra. She was Beauty. Cute, but Cacophonic: While not 'cacophonic', the most memorable part of Christa is that she sounds like she has a perpetual cold. Everyone Loves Blondes: Inverted as She apparently hated alotaround camp: the reason Drake threw immunity challenge? To get her out. Ryno's throwaway vote in his boot episode? For Christa. Who was blamed for sabotaging the tribe after Rupert was blindsided? Christa. You just had to feel sorry for the poor girl when she had most of the camp apart from her trio plotting against her. Hidden Depths: She was apparently such good friends with Sandra and Rupert, that when Rupert was blindsided, she plotted with Sandra toburn the shelter down.

characters.name: Tijuana Bradley
characters.description: Bullying a Dragon: The moment she starts trying to tell Fairplay what he can or can't do, she finds herself promptly voted out. Idiot Ball: Causes her own elimination by getting too greedy. Irony: In thevery first episodeNicole tries to get Tijuana out, but gets a little greedy with the vote, resulting in her elimination. In her boot episode, she does the same thing, and is eliminated for it. Mooning: Done unintentionally during a couple challenges. Only Known by Their Nickname: "T".

characters.name: Rupert Boneham
characters.description: Rupert would come back to compete inAll-Stars,Heroes Vs. Villains, andBlood Vs. Water. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: With Sandra and Christa. He was Brawn. Berserk Button: Jon and Trish voting for him sets off an absolute shitstorm that Jon takes the brunt of. Beware the Nice Ones: He may be aGentle Giant, but he's an emotional guy, and his angry moments are as intense as the happy ones. Brains Evil, Brawn Good: Compared to Johnny Fairplay.

characters.name: Ryan "Ryno" Opray
characters.description: Friend to All Living Things: Andrew stated that Ryan liked animals during Pelican Pete's visit. Number Two: He was Andrew's right hand man throughout the entire time he stayed. Known Only by Their Nickname: "Ryno", which comes from "Ryan O.". Tall, Dark, and Handsome Worthy Opponent: While voting for Ryan to leave, Rupert laments the fact that he has to vote Ryan out, saying that he wished that he could trade a few of his tribe members (most likely Burton and Jon) for guys like him.

characters.name: Andrew Savage
characters.description: Savage got voted back in by the public to compete inCambodia: Second Chance. Badass in a Nice Suit: Justified, as he was only taking the clothes on his back. Berserk Button: When Jon, while 'looting' the Morgan camp, tells Andrew that Drake actually threw the first challenge Morgan won, Andrew not only doesn't believe him, but reviles the idea so much that he propels Morgan to victory in the next immunity challenge. Diabolus ex Machina: If it weren't for Burton and Lil coming back, he almost undoubtedly would have made the jury, possibly even the finals. But, they came back, aligned with the former Drake tribe at the merge, and sent him packing. Thank Goodness he was chosen to compete onSurvivor: Cambodia Ensemble Dark Horse: The reason why he was brought back for Cambodia.

characters.name: Osten Taylor
characters.description: Animals Hate Him: Inverted.Hehates animals, especially pelicans. The Big Guy: For Morgan. Whenever there's some sort of strength challenge, the weight (metaphorically and literally) falls on his shoulders. Butt-Monkey: He sold off all his clothes, except for his boxers, in the first day. This is most likely the reason why the island took its toll on him. Irony: The toughest looking guy in his season ends up being the biggest wimp and the show's first official quitter. In addition, it was revealed post-show that he quit due to a staph infection that was never fully addressed on the show, making the poor edit and treatment he got for quitting look likeDisproportionate Retributionin hindsight, considering how the revelation makes him one of the more justifiable quitters among those who have quit the game and some non-medical quitters have received better edits and treatment than him (most of the later players who quit for medical reasons have received much more generous edits, with Probst even publicly backing some in interviews). Non-Gameplay Elimination: Osten was the first person to quit Survivor.

characters.name: Shawn Cohen
characters.description: Disc-One Final Boss: Certainly for Jon. Jerk Jock: He and Burton act like stereotypical jocks making fun of the weird kids, which is something that Rupert especially didn't like. Afterwards, Jon was the recipient of his ire. Lazy Bum: He got called out on it many times by his tribe. He had many arguments with Jon over his lack of work ethic. Small Name, Big Ego: According to his CBS bio, his friends and family like to call him "World's Greatest Salesman" or something similar. He seemed to believe this, despite being even more disliked on his tribe than Jonny Fairplay. The Quisling: First by betraying Burton, then by betraying Trish. Not that he had much of a choice with Burton, however.

characters.name: Trish Dunn
characters.description: I Coulda Been a Contender!: In possibly the best position possible strategic-wise - everyone liked her, she had a good alliance with Fairplay andShawn, and was extremely close to eliminating a potential post-merge threat (Rupert) - if Sandra hadn't ratted her out, and Shawn hadn't flipped back to the triumvirate, Trish could have taken control of the game. Incompatible Orientation/Oblivious to Love: In the first episode, a store woman develops a crush on Trish, she does not pick up on it, but Sandra does. The Starscream: Made a failed attempt just before the merge to overthrow the Rupert/Christa/Sandra triumvirate on Drake by recruiting Drake's most hated members, Jon and Shawn, into voting out Rupert. Shawn initially agrees with the plan, but later changes his mind, which leads to a 4-2 vote out against Trish.

characters.name: Michelle Tesauro
characters.description: The Cutie: On Drake, there was a three member alliance (four if Jonny Fairplay had joined up with them), consisting ofBurton,Shawnand Michelle. Hoist By Her Own Petard: The plan during the food-eating competition mentioned below was for Michelle to fake being disgusted by the food and get it down as slow as possible, so she would get chosen for the tiebreaker by Morgan, after which she would scoff it down faster than anyone. Unfortunately for her, she got it down way too fast, Morgan chose Sandra, who ACTUALLY had trouble, that lost them the challenge, and Michelle was left to take the blame. Bye-bye, Michelle. The Ingenue: She was portrayed as sweet and innocent and therefore was probably cast for theIngénuearchetypical role for which Colleen Haskell is the prototype. Revenge: While this applies to all the Outcasts, she was the one who vocalized it the most. Tomboy: Admits to loving to eat and drink gross things, and proves it during the food eating competition in Episode 5.

characters.name: "Skinny" Ryan Shoulders
characters.description: Intergenerational Friendship: With Lillian. Telling that both of them voted for each other to get back into the game. Geek Physiques: There's a reason his tribemates called himSkinny Ryanwhile on the show. The Load: Was beyond useless at challenges.

characters.name: Nicole Delma
characters.description: The Complainer Is Always Wrong: Was annoyed with Tijuana and tried to organized an alliance to boot her. This caused Nicole to get the boot instead. Graceful Loser: In her final words. Honor Before Reason: Used against her - her tribe kicked her off for trying to organize the blindside of Morgan's obviously weaker members. Ms. Fanservice: Lampshaded by Jeff during the premiere, saying she might be popular because she wasn't wearing a bra. Too Clever by Half: She attempted to eliminate a threat in the form of Tijuana instead of one of the easy votes like Ryan S. or Lillian. The tribe booted her to restore order.

characters.name: Saboga
characters.description: A House Divided: At first from internal drama, then from literal breaking apart into other tribes. Once they hit the merge, only Jenna Lewis and Rupert remain. They donotjoin an alliance together. The Artifact: Was dissolved into the other two tribes early on as the result of losing a specific challenge. The Bus Came Back: Like everyone else this season. Dwindling Party: Saboga lost two-thirds of the their original tribe members in the tribal phase, with only Rupert and Jenna L. left come the merge. Epic Fail: Though not as bad as others, Saboga lost the first two immunity challenges and had the worst shelter of the tribes.

characters.name: Chapera
characters.description: The Ace: The strongest of the three tribes, only losing two immunity challenges in the entire season. By the merge, they only lost two members, and by the end, Boston Rob and Amber were in a power position to make it to the final tribal council. A House Divided: In the merge. The Bus Came Back: Like the rest of the season. Law of Chromatic Superiority: Chapera is the red colored tribe and proved to be the strongest of the three tribes. My Greatest Second Chance: Played straight by Amber and Boston Rob, as well as by Alicia.

characters.name: Mogo Mogo
characters.description: Always Second Best: It's brought up by Colby that this was something that actually served them well during the beginning of the season when three tribes were present, as they were often able to do just well enough to stay ahead of at least one of the other tribes in challenges and avoid the severe consequences that would befall the last-place finisher. In the earliest stage of the game, they're the only one of the three tribes that avoided going to Tribal Council, only losing Jenna because she quit to be with her ailing mother. However, once the Saboga tribe is dissolved, leaving only two tribes left to compete in challenges, this comes back to hurt them. They find themselves unable to best the Chapera tribe in the majority of competitions, whittling their numbers down to the point that they come into the merge with a sizable disadvantage that they aren't able to overcome (even with Kathy and Shii Ann's individual immunity wins). Badass Crew: Subverted. The tribe was stacked with some of the best challenge competitors evernoteIn their original seasons Colby won eight individual challenges, Lex won five, Jenna won four, Kathy won four and Richard won one for a total of twenty-two, as opposed to Saboga's six and Chapera's two.but before Saboga's dissolve they consistently come in second place while after the dissolve they go on a losing streak. The Bus Came Back: Like the rest of the season. Dwindling Party: It wasn't too bad at the start, only losing Jenna M. due to her withdrawal, but things began snowballing downhill after the tribe absorption. Of the original Mogo Mogo members, Richard and Colby were sent home in their next tribal councils, and come the merge, the three remaining members were taken out one by one until Shi-Ann was sent to the jury at the final six. The more surprising point to make is that all of Mogo Mogo were taken outbeforeSaboga, the weakest tribe of the three. Idiot Ball: Voting out Jerri over Amber to appease Boston Rob.

characters.name: Rudy Boesch
characters.description: Determinator: He was, and remains, the oldest contestant to appear on Survivor, with no one eclipsing either of his appearances. Game-Breaking Injury: He was already in a perilous position due to being 75 years old, but after he injured his ankle during a challenge he was considered to be too great a detriment to the tribe and was voted out. Intergenerational Friendship: With Rupert. Odd Couple: As inBorneo, Rudy's best friend on the tribe is the last person you'd expect. This time it's the tie-dyed bearded hippie-looking Rupert, who immediately bonds with Rudy over their shared sense of honor. Unfortunately this partnership ends before it really begins when Rudy is voted out (against Rupert's protests). Squick: When he drinks the unboiled water, despite being told that it has parasites that will put him in a coma. His justification is even worse: InVietnamhe drank water from a reservoir that had half a dozen bodies floating in it at any time. If he could drink that and survive he's not scared of well water in Panama.

characters.name: Yasur
characters.description: A House Divided: But not as neatly as Lopevi's case. Amazon Brigade: The original line-up and still pretty much this after the swap. Divided We Fall: When the merge hit, everything was set in place for them to dominate the rest of the game, and they proceeded to pagong the Lopevi tribe until there was one member left. However, underlying tensions ultimately broke them apart. Twila, Scout, and Eliza teamed up with Chris to eliminate Ami's Yasur Alliance, leaving the door open for him to win the remaining immunity challenges of the season and ultimately take the title of Sole Survivor for himself. Location Theme Naming: Named after a Mount Yasur, a volcano in Vanuatu. Total Party Kill: No one from the second iteration of Yasur made it to Day 39.

characters.name: Lopevi
characters.description: A House Divided: From the very first episode they were strictly divided into the "Fit Four" (mostly younger players) and the "Fat Five" (a counter-alliance mostly of older players). The more numerous Fat Five obviously outlasted the Fit Four. Dwindling Party: Entered the merge with fewer numbers and had already lost many early immunities. Besides Chris, all of them were gone by the final 7. Law of Chromatic Superiority: After the swap, they won most of the challenges and produced both the winner and the runner up. Location Theme Naming: Named after a volcanic island in Vanuatu.

characters.name: Alinta
characters.description: A House Divided: Very few people made alliances with people from another tribe. Law of Chromatic Superiority: The tribe color is orange, fitting with the prior two tribes yellow and red.

characters.name: Chris Daugherty
characters.description: Anti-Hero: Particularly for guys. Badass Boast: This line in the penultimate episode showed us just how much control he had in the game:I don't trust Scout, I don't trust Twila, I don't trust Eliza, I don't trust Julie. And they don't trust each other. And the most screwed-up thing about it is I think they all trustme. Best Served Cold: His elimination of Julie. She betrayed the men's alliance and caused the elimination of Rory, Sarge and Chad. In revenge Chris lied to her the whole game, making promises and reassuring her just hours before her elimination even when it would have no benefit for his own game, just to engineer the most potent blindside possible. The Chessmaster: Was the brains of the older alliance at Lopevi, and later managed to maneuver himself to win the game despite being outnumbered 6-1. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Particularly to Julie and Eliza.

characters.name: Twila Tanner
characters.description: Break the Haughty: A very abrasive person throughout the entirety of the season, she entered the final tribal council mostly unrepentant for her words and actions, even telling Eliza that she sucked (a guaranteed way to not get a vote). At the end, she's reduced to tears having realized she hurt so many people. Brutal Honesty: In general, but especially at Final Tribal Council. It still earned her votes, as she didn't have BS up to her ears. Cool Old Lady: A hardworking tomboy who holds her own with people half her age. Distaff Counterpart: To Chris. They're both boisterous blue collar workers from the Midwest who struggle to relate to their younger tribemates. They even work in the same field. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Her son James.

characters.name: Scout Cloud Lee
characters.description: But Not Too Gay: She kissed her partner during the challenge, but it was cut out. Cool Old Lady: Scout was the oldest castaway of the season and managed to avoid being voted out despite being a liability in challenges. Her social maneuvering granted her the fallen angel title. Cool Shades: They help show off herCool Old Ladyvibes. Grumpy Old Woman: When dealing with Eliza, though generally well-liked by the rest of the cast. Ice-Cream Koan: Delivers a couple of these during her tribal council votes, most notably when she votes for Julie and tells her to "return to her roots" (which hints at herNative heritage).

characters.name: Eliza Orlins
characters.description: Eliza would later return as a fan-favorite forMicronesia: Fans Vs. Favorites. All of the Other Reindeer: As elegantly put by herself, for all of Vanuatu she was really working with an alliance of herself, and... well, just herself. Annoying Younger Sibling: How all her other tribemates perceived her, but at least Ami emphasizes the "little sibling" part over the "annoying" part. And, like most of them, she never got favor with the Lopevis. Badass Adorable: On the chopping block since the very first day. Lasted all the way to fourth. Butt-Monkey: Everyone found her annoying and was always in danger of being sent home. She just wants to have friends and feel safe!

characters.name: Julie Berry
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: As the Lopevi men soon found out. Braids, Beads and Buckskins: Yes, she is Indigenous. Break the Cutie: Chris's betrayal of her. Broken Tears: At final tribal council. Femme Fatale: Her Survivor casting archetype

characters.name: Ami Cusack
characters.description: Ami would later return as a fan-favorite forMicronesia: Fans Vs. Favorites. Action Girl: One of the better physical competitors and also being great at puzzles, earning her only immunity necklace because of one. Anti-Villain: For the most part it's really just the way the game plays out that makes her the villain; aside from a moment here or there she's really not much worse than Chris. Arc Villain: To theAmazon Brigade. Ami's role as the season's chiefStraw Feministcomes into focus around the time of the tribe swap (where she underlines the "men vs. women" mentality) and lasts through her elimination at the Final 6. Once she's gone, the narrative shifts more to Chris having to decide whether to side more with the pairing of Eliza and Julie or Scout and Twila as his final endgame competitors. The Baroness: She’s in charge and is rather haughty about it.

characters.name: Leann Slaby
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: She's dreadful in swimming challenges, costing her team at least one challenge because she gave up. Brainy Brunette: As an equity research assistant and the alleged brains of the women's alliance, she is this. The Dragon: To Ami.Dragon-in-Chief: If post-game interviews are to be believed. Dragon-in-Chief: If post-game interviews are to be believed. Exact Words: She voted for Chris because she told Twila that she'd never write her name down.

characters.name: James "Chad" Crittenden
characters.description: Artificial Limbs: His leg, as a result of a tumor. Chad is also the first amputee on the show. Badass Teacher: His job outside of the game, and is also a good competitor. Handicapped Badass: So much so that he was voted out for being a physical threat. Informed Flaw: He is associated with the Fat Five, but he's in great shape and is just as young as the fit four. He might have been lumped in with them because his artificial leg could be a disadvantage, but that condition is largely irrelevant to his successes and failures. Inspirationally Disadvantaged: He got a rare form a cancer that caused his amputation. John Kenney was even worried about taking him to the final two because invoking this trope would probably net him a lot of points.

characters.name: Lea "Sarge" Masters
characters.description: The Ace: Has a wide set of survival skills and isn’t a bad strategist either. Death Glare: When Scout starts singing to him mockingly the day after Rory was voted off. Probably qualifies as aFunny Moment. Drill Sergeant Nasty: Subverted; he was only this in a challenge where he had to call upon it to lead the tribe. Otherwise he was a pretty good guy. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Virtually nobody refers to him as Lea. He’s “Sarge”. Gender-Blender Name: How it's spelled, anyway. Probably why he goes by "Sarge".

characters.name: Rory Freeman
characters.description: The Complainer Is Always Wrong: Early on, as his temper gets on the nerves of just about everyone. Later, when he’s up against Ami’s callous treatment, the show depicts his complaining as being more legitimate. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: The moment you put a slingshot in his hands, watch out. Hair-Trigger Temper: One of his defining characteristics is that he goes off at the slightest hitch. His wife even points this out her letter to him. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: His bad temper and stand-offish nature put a lot of people off, but his friendship with Bubba and his reactions during the letter reward show a much softer side. "No More Holding Back" Speech: The morning after Bubba's elimination, Rory digs deep and gives them an incredibly cheesy speech, apologizing for his anger and promising to do better.

characters.name: John Kenney
characters.description: Dumb Muscle: Subverted. SeeSmarter Than You Look. Last of His Kind: The very last member of the Fit Four alliance. Lazy Bum: His boot episode paints him as this, but is attributed to him knowing that he's the next on the chopping block. Mr. Fanservice: John was a model at the time of filming, and he continued his modeling career afterwards. The One Guy: Temporarily when he was sent to Yasur to study them.

characters.name: Lisa Keiffer
characters.description: Disproportionate Retribution: On the receiving end of this. She accidentally implies that she might be gunning for Ami and gets booted off as a result. Freudian Slip: When gathering food with Ami, Lisa asked how to gather food in case Ami was no longer there. Ami picked up on this and arranged for her oust. Out of Focus: Gets rather limited screen time proportional to how many episodes she's been in. Shocking Elimination: At leastIn-Universe. Given Ami being aStraw Feministand Rory being male, one naturally assumed that he was the one going, not her. Twila outright said they were expecting Rory to go.

characters.name: Travis "Bubba" Sampson
characters.description: Good Ol' Boy: A friendly, hard-working family-man with a strong southern accent. Happily Married: He mentions how much he misses his wife and kids several times. Nice Guy: Very friendly with all of Lopevi and tries to make friends at Yasur too, though Ami shuts that down. Only Known by Their Nickname: Bubba Sacrificial Lamb: His elimination is the beginning of Ami's rise to power.

characters.name: Brady Finta
characters.description: Older Than They Look: Despite being a member of the younger men's alliance, Brady was 33 and a few months older than Bubba. Only Sane Man: The most levelheaded member of the young guys alliance. Tall, Dark, and Snarky

characters.name: Mia Galeotalanza
characters.description: Hair-Trigger Temper: She admits to this in the rites of passage. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: To Twila Unsportsman Like Gloating: In the first reward challenge, shemoonwalkedto the finish.

characters.name: John "J.P." Palyok
characters.description: Ascended Fanboy: John applied for Pearl Islands and was recruited for this season. I Coulda Been a Contender! Malaproper: Was frequently butchering words, most famously confusing "ember and "amber". Tall, Dark, and Handsome

characters.name: Dolly Neely
characters.description: Conditioned to Accept Horror: A pig is slaughtered during the premiere and she doesn't flinch. She says it's because she raises sheep for a living, so she's used to it. Everyone Loves Blondes: Most everyone adores her; her vote-out was almost entirely strategy. Farm Girl: And dressed like theFarmer's Daughter, too. The Ingenue: Seems to have been cast for this role, of which Colleen fromBorneois the prototype. Ms. Fanservice: Brief though her time was, her cuteness was certainly noticed.

characters.name: Brook Geraghty
characters.description: Ascended Fanboy: To the point of asking to for another chance at the reunion. The Complainer Is Always Wrong: Lobbied the hardest for Chris to be voted out; it caused the majority alliance to turn on him instead. Death by Genre Savviness: Was the first guy voted out for being the only younger man on Lopevi (there was an age war going on at the time) to have watched the show previously. He even called himself a super fan of Survivor in his bio. Gender-Blender Name: "Brook," (though much more commonly spelled "Brooke,") is a common girls' name. I Coulda Been a Contender!: As he says at the reunion, he had bigger plans if he had made it past the first few days.

characters.name: Ulong
characters.description: Adam and Eve Plot: Only Stephenie and Bobby Jon remained. They also got chosen to be team captains next season. Always Need What You Gave Up: In their first Tribal Council, they chose to vote out Jolanda because they felt she was too bossy. This turned out to be a fatal mistake aslack of real leadership was what lead to them failing. Even worse,they refused to believe it. Butt-Monkey: One of the biggest in the series, bar none. Can't Catch Up: After making a few very poor choices in what tribemates they wanted in their tribe, they lost Jeff when he went walking and stepped on something that led to him taking aSuicide by Copelimination, and this was the straw that broke their back. Crippling Overspecialization: The tribe's only true "strengths" was just their raw physicality and nothing else, as they severely lacked leadership, communication, and cohesion, resulting in loss after loss after loss.

characters.name: Koror
characters.description: The Ace: The tribe in general had some of the strongest players, some great puzzle solvers, and such a fantastic team dynamic that they never lost asingleimmunity challenge! A House Divided: Once it came to the jury phase. Badass Crew: As stated before, Koror had some strong members that led to a sweep in immunity challenges. Tom and Ian were the front runners in challenges, Greg was very physically strong, and Coby was the expert in puzzle solving. The fact that the majority of the tribe were in their forties helped them make more thought out strategies to lead into victories. Born Winners: It probably wasn't seen at first when the tribes were made, but Koror ended up not only sweeping all the Immunity Challenges, but they eventually produced the winner of the season. The Dreaded: As the season went out, it was becoming clear to Ulong that trying to defeat Koror wasn't as easy as they thought.

characters.name: Tom Westman
characters.description: Tom would compete again inHeroes Vs. Villains. The Ace: Tom won five immunity challenges, the most of any winner.noteThis tiesColby'sachievement of most immunity wins in a single season.Terry,Ozzy,Mike, andBradwould also win 5 immunity wins in their seasons. Mike is the only one besides Tom to also win his season.He also (along with Ian and Gregg) carried Koror to a unanimous win over Ulong throughout the pre-merge. Action Hero: The equivalent in Survivor. He's one of the few challenge beasts to make it all the way to the end and win. Born Winner: Name one winner in the fourty plus seasons that was on the most dominate tribe in the show's history and never received a vote against him. Cool Old Guy: Tom was in his forties by the time he competed.

characters.name: Katie Gallagher
characters.description: Break the Haughty: She was clearly not expecting everybody to hate her so much when she came into tribal. Can't Take Criticism: In the final tribal council, she was openly hostile to the jurors who criticized her, and even refused to answer a question that would have required her to list her own negative qualities.Seeing how Katie needed four of the seven jury votes to win,it goes almost exactly how you'd expect. Deadpan Snarker: This is her brand of humor and what she thought everyone saw her as. The Friend Nobody Likes: Just listen to what everyone on the jury has to say about her. Humiliation Conga: Final Jury wasn't exactly a pleasant experience for her. But shedidtake it in stride at the reunion.

characters.name: Ian Rosenberger
characters.description: The Atoner: Spends his last few days trying to repair his damaged trust with Katie, then Tom. He finally gets it back viaHeroic Sacrificeat the final immunity challenge. The Baby of the Bunch: It's easy to forget given his height and deep voice but Ian is the youngest castmate at 23 and on a tribe of many people in their 40's. His age shows the most with his sensitivity as he takes other people's opinions of him to heart, a trait that leads to his eventual forfeit Dying Moment of Awesome: He uses his elimination to mend fences with both Katie and Tom. This act propels him from a good character to a legendary character. Friend to All Living Things: He works as a dolphin trainer, and apologizes sincerely to a large snake before he kills it for it's meat. Honor Before Reason: Very much willing to play dirty, but his conscience was so strong he gave up his game for the really quite minimal betrayals and lies he told.

characters.name: Jenn Lyon
characters.description: Guile Heroine: The deleted scenes show Jenn being a lot more cunning than she was portrayed during the show. Out of Focus: She was practically invisible during the premerge. This can be explained by Koror having never gone to tribal council, but characters like Ian, Tom, and Gregg still get screen time. Overshadowed by Awesome: She wasn't a slouch in challenges, stepping up against Stephenie (the most athletic female on the season), but she had no shot in hell against Ian and Tom. Plucky Girl: Once Gregg was out of the picture, she was clearly on the bottom as she had been blindsided. She made her way to the finale if that counts. The Rival: Often found herself matched up against Stephenie during physical challenges. Jeff even refers to her as this.

characters.name: Caryn Groedel
characters.description: Idiot Ball: Telling Tom of the plot to vote him out. Laser-Guided Karma: Caryn told Tom about the Women's alliance. This would not protect her from being voted out at the final 5. Manipulative Bastard: At the schoolyard pick on day two. She chose Willard, an older guy who shows signs of being grumpy, over Johnathan, who is young and athletic, because she knew the tribe would vote Willard out before her. This decision would become true and it (along with Koror being so dominant) got her to the merge. Spanner in the Works: To the Girls alliance.

characters.name: Gregg Carey
characters.description: The Big Guy: Though Ian and Tom are just as physical as he is, if not moreso, they fall much more neatly underThe LancerandThe Leadertropes better. Instead, he serves this role to Koror and later their personal alliance. Genius Bruiser: Aside from being one of Koror's better physical assets, he was also constantly in motion and strategizing with Jenn. Overshadowed by Awesome: He was very strategically, physically, and socially capable in his own right, but Tom and Ian were both flashier in these regards and managed to outplay him, so he's often left out of conversations of strongest player of the season. The Rival: Gregg and Ian were the only ones who would ever stand a chance against Tom in the finals, which is why Tom blindsides him the first chance he gets. Ship Tease: With Jenn.

characters.name: StephenieLaGrossa
characters.description: Stephenie would return for a third time onHeroes Vs. Villains. Accentuate the Negative: It only takes a couple of challenge losses for Stephenie to start comparing her tribe toUlong, which is a fairly harsh comparison seeing as that was thesingle least successful tribe in Survivor history. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Her hair was notably dyed darker here. Big Eater: The one thing that everybody seemed to agree on, whether they were on her side or not, is that Stephanie never, ever stopped eating. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Hadnoset allegiances this time around.

characters.name: Janu Tornell
characters.description: Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She found herself on the outs rather quickly, some in part to her not being very sociable. Butt-Monkey: She's got sick quickly and didn't acclimatize to the island as well as the rest of her tribe. Since she was mopey, the tribe wasn't fond of her, which fed on her mopeyness. Despair Event Horizon: There is a point where she breaks down and stops having fun, laying in her hammock all day with a tired face and tear-stained eyes. Foreshadowing: Coby puts a lot of emphasis on her quitting at one point. She does so after his elimination. Heroic Sacrifice: Quitting to save Stephenie.

characters.name: Coby Archa
characters.description: Camp Gay: He's an effeminate man who works as a hairdresser, so one may say this applies to him. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: He wasn't particularly in shape and is an effeminate gay man, but he was very capable during challenges. Dark and Troubled Past: Being a gay man before it becoming relatively accepted, Coby brings up a history of exclusion and bullying as a result of his identity. Deadpan Snarker: He made it very clear that he disliked most of the people on his tribe. Gag Penis: Maybe the only contestant on the show's history to wear really skimpy speedos instead of swim shorts.

characters.name: Bobby Jon Drinkard
characters.description: Bobby Jon would return for a second chance inGuatemala. Break the Badass: The multiple challenge losses started getting to him when he and Steph were the only people left. Steph notes that he started operating on autopilot. Breakout Character: To the point that he was immediately brought back for the following season as one of the series's team captains. Determinator: Just like Steph, even though his heart started breaking from the numerous losses, he gave his heart in everything he did. Elimination by Irony: Taught Stephenie how to make fire. It became his undoing in his last tribal council. Stephenie herself even lampshades it afterwards, stating that he taught her so well that she ended up beating him.

characters.name: Ibrehem Rahman
characters.description: My Greatest Failure: He blew one of Ulong's only leads because he couldn't find a bottle, and it haunts him for the remainder of his time on Survivor. Koror purposely gave him immunity for it, and forced them to scramble at one tribal council during the last minute. Out of Focus: Had the least visibility out of the final three Ulong members, have being overshadowed before by Kim and Jeff. Paper Tiger: He's one of the biggest and strongest people on the season, but his challenge performance is a mixed bag. Religious Bruiser: Providedsomephysicality during challenges and his Islamic faith is a big facet of his character. Tempting Fate: Thought that Ulong's raw strength would crush Koror at the beginning. Oh, how wrong was he!

characters.name: James Miller
characters.description: Becoming the Mask: It's hard to tell whether or not his stereotypical "redneck" behaviour is an act or not. One minute he's speaking pretty normally to theConfession Cam, and the next he's giving some bizarre homespun speech to the tribe that only he can understand. Establishing Character Moment: The veryfirstconfessional of the season was him calling Jeff a son-of-a-bitch. Politically Incorrect Hero: For a given value of "hero", since Ulong was the group of plucky underdogs. A lot of James's comments come off pretty bigoted. Rage Against the Author: In the very first confessional of the season, James vented his frustration with Jeff Probst after the latter announced to the starting cast that they would have to row their way to the beach in an attempt to grab individual immunity.James:Jeff is a son of a bitch, I'll tell you that. Southern-Fried Genius: He tried to be this but most certainly wasn't.

characters.name: Cassandra Ann "Angie" Jakusz
characters.description: Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Was nearly voted out in the first Tribal Council for being perceived as a weak player. She was not, and actually turned out to be one of Ulong's strongest players in challenges. Diabolus ex Machina: While not a new twist by any means, had Koror not been given the opportunity to hand immunity to Ibrehemspecificallybecause he was in trouble, Angie could have lasted a little while longer. Then, the vote winds up tied and she and Bobby Jon are unable to vote again. She gets sent packing the instant everyone else's options get narrowed down. Fag Hag: During the first day, she and Coby seemed to be friends because they had a shared history of exclusion. Seemed to be, until Coby passed her over during the tribal selection process. Angie was slightly devastated by it. According to him, he passed her over because he didn't want the two of them to be on the outs because of their "alternative" lifestyles. Ms. Fanservice: If you're into her archetype, she has a very tiny swimsuit. Perky Goth: Most of the time, anyway.

characters.name: Willard Smith
characters.description: Irony: The guyPicked Lastfor Koror got eliminated on the same at night as Angie, the girl last picked for Ulong. Out of Focus: He didn't get a lot of screen time, but post-show interviews and certain deleted scenes have hinted that the guy was aDeadpan SnarkerandCool Old Guy. Running Joke: Some viewers thought that Willard looked like Palau's version of the immunity idol. It gets called the "immunity Willard" to this day, far past his elimination when the show was airing. Sacrificial Lamb: He was the victim of Koror's only tribal council because he was old. Self-Deprecation: He refers to himself as an old curmudgeon.

characters.name: Kim Mullen
characters.description: Broken Bird: She recognizes fairly quickly that Ulong is a doomed tribe, but accepts her fate and doesn't do too much to save herself. The Cassandra: It's a lack of a clear leader she believes is the source of Ulong's failures, with no one stepping up to the plate. Of course, nobody listens to her because they all think she sucks. The Complainer Is Always Wrong: She complained about Ulong's dysfunctions and lack of cohesiveness. Not that she everdidanything about it though. Everybody Loves Blondes: Averted. Everyone thought she sucked and her name was tossed out as early as episode 2. The Load: Was rarely useful in challenges, and spent the second immunity challenge on the pontoon instead of helping. They also note she doesn't work as much in camp, reasoning that they should conserve their energy for challenges.

characters.name: Jeff Wilson
characters.description: Defeating the Undefeatable: In his final episode, Jeff managed to hand Tom one of his few defeats in a head-on challenge by scoring a point on him during the "By Any Means Necessary" reward challenge. Game-Breaking Injury: Rolling his foot on a coconut. This not only cost him his game, it cost Ulong their game when they proved that as far as competing with Koror went,We Cannot Go On Without You. Heroic Sacrifice: He decided to leave the game because his injury made him a liability. Even though Kim sucked at challenges, she could at the very leastwalk. The Rival: He was the only person on Ulong who could keep up against Tom from Koror in the challenges. Ship Tease: With Kim.

characters.name: Ashlee Ashby
characters.description: Alliterative NameBonus points for being the first syllable of each name repeated, not just the first sound or letter. The Ingenue: In her pre-season CBS written bio, it talked about how "A practicing Mormon, she is most proud of graduating from seminary for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints while still in high school. It required that she get up every day at 5:00 am to drive 30 minutes to the church to study the bible and church teachings before school." Her religious faith was very important to her, so it is likely Ashlee was cast for the archetypical role of theIngénue. Neleh Dennis was another young Mormon woman cast for thatIngénuerole six seasons prior. Ms. Fanservice: For the brief time she was around. Suicide by Cop: Asked to be voted out because of her ensuing illness. Her request was not shown on TV.

characters.name: Jolanda Jones
characters.description: The Ace: She's an accomplished athlete inReal Life, and showed off her track skills by winning one of the two individual immunity necklaces during the first day (the other being Ian). Alliterative Name:JolandaJones. Black Boss Lady: For Ulong and why she was voted out. Voting out someone they thought could win at such an early stage of the game turned out to be a critical error. Dark and Troubled Past: Mentioned in herCBS profileJolanda had a hard childhood. Disappeared Dad: Her fatherCommitted Suicidewhen Jolanda was only a year old.

characters.name: Wanda Shirk
characters.description: Chewing the Scenery: Oh god, her singing. Cool Old Lady: The oldest woman of the season.

characters.name: Jonathan Libby
characters.description: Hidden Depths: Jonathan beat out cancer. We Hardly Knew Ye: Why was he eliminated on the second day? We'll probably never know, but Angie did hint at the Reunion that he was a bit of aJerkass.

characters.name: Yaxhá
characters.description: Dwindling Party: Post-swap Yaxhá were eliminated right at the merge, with only Danni left against five post-swap Nakúms. Failure Tribe: Though not as bad as most, Yaxha (both incarnations) generally lost challenges. Meaningful Name: Means means blue-green water in an unspecified Mayan language.

characters.name: Nakúm
characters.description: Curb-Stomp Battle: Especially before the tribe swap. Meaningful Name: Means "cooking house/ house of the pot" in an unspecified Mayan language

characters.name: Danielle "Danni" Boatwright
characters.description: Danni would invited back forWinners at War. Advantage Ball: Danni bid and won a challenge advantage at the Survivor Auction, which allowed her to swap places with someone at anytime in the Squared Off Challenge. It helped her immensely as a timely move to swap places with Stephenie won her immunity. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl Ascended Fangirl: To Gary Hogeboom. Dark Horse Victory: Seemed to have no shot post-merge and yet managed to claw her way to the final two and win. It helps that she won a few immunity challenges and the majority alliance started taking each other out due to multiple reasons.

characters.name: Rafe Judkins
characters.description: Ascended Fanboy: One of two superfans of the show this season (the other being Brian) who have watched and studied Survivor since their youth. Honor Before Reason: Twice; first by ensuring Danni made the final three and not Lydia because of their agreement to get that far, and then to actually tell her it was okay to not honor their agreement to get to the final two because Stephenie had tried so hard in the final challenge. Though to be fair, it was established that Stephenie would never win a jury vote and would be taken no matter what, so Rafe releasing Danni from their agreement was really a formality at that rate. Nice Guy: He was always concerned about other people's feelings. When Jamie would try to rub it in post-swap Yaxha's faces when they'd lose, Rafe did not like that. He also released Danni from the promise to go to final two, which was a very Mr. Nice Guy kind of thing to do. Smart People Wear Glasses Straight Gay: Rafe is gay but his mannerisms and attitude aren't the stereotypical kind of male gay one would peg him as.

characters.name: Lydia Morales
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: Her singing and dancing were pretty fun. Out of Focus: Has a couple of moments but mostly just sort of stays off to the sidelines, being kept in the game because she was incapable of winning anything. Though according to Rafe the editreallydidn't do her personality justice. Shout-Out: Does an impression of Keenan Ivory Wayans as Little Richard onIn Living Color!at one point. Team Mom: Of Stephenie's alliance.

characters.name: Cindy Hall
characters.description: Friend to All Living Things: A zookeeper, and she was delighted by the local wildlife, in contrast to the rest of the tribe. Laser-Guided Karma: Laser Guided Carma: Wins the car challenge and is given the choice of keeping the car or giving it up and letting the other four get cars instead, in order to ward off the notorious "Car Curse." She decides to keep it, saying she can beat the odds and overcome the curse.Guess what happens next. Male Gaze: There’s a shot of her rear in the intro, no less. Ms. Fanservice: SeeMale Gazeabove. Rewarded as a Traitor Deserves: Chose to keep her car instead of giving the other four tribemates cars, and this decision alone manages to keep the infamous "Car Curse" alive when the others, who were really unimpressed with this, put her on the wrong side of the voting road.

characters.name: Judd Sergeant (IV)
characters.description: AAAAY DEEEE... Ooh, Shiny! Bad Liar: Gary notices he's looking upwards when the guy says the idol is on the ground.The clue he gets basically says "the Idol is in a tree" so he tells the tribe "It is definitely, by far, on the ground".Later at tribal council he says he has never told a lie, when Gary points out he lied about the idol clue he says "okay, so I told one lie." The clue he gets basically says "the Idol is in a tree" so he tells the tribe "It is definitely, by far, on the ground". Later at tribal council he says he has never told a lie, when Gary points out he lied about the idol clue he says "okay, so I told one lie." Big Brother Instinct: Towards Jamie

characters.name: Gary Hogeboom
characters.description: Celebrity Survivor: Among the earliest examples. Cool Old Guy: The oldest person on Yaxha and the first person to find the hidden immunity idol. Paper-Thin Disguise: An ex-NFL quarterback pretends to just be an ordinary landscaper in a game where another player (the eventual winner, by the way) is a sports reporter-Hilarity Ensues. Amazingly, though, he doesn't really get stigmatized for that. Retired Badass: Former NFL Quarterback.

characters.name: Jamie Newton
characters.description: Jerk with a Heart of Gold Large Ham: By proxy of imitating Bobby Jon. Odd Friendship: WithJudd,BrianandLydia. And, once on the jury with him, Bobby Jon. Properly Paranoid: Subverted; his paranoia that he's going to get blindsided early wears on everyone so much that theyfulfill his prophecy for him. The Rival: To Bobby Jon. Especially during hisscreaming matchwith Bobby Jon.

characters.name: Brandon Bellinger
characters.description: Farm Boy: Brandon's occupation is a farmer. Foil: Becomes this to Jamie during his boot episode. Good Ol' Boy: Brandon's casting archetype is this. His pre-season bio video was all about his country background in Kansas. Some other men who were cast for the sameGood Old Boycharacter trope in other seasons are Rodger Bingham, Big Tom Buchanan, Travis 'Bubba' Sampson, James Clement, Boo Bernis, Chicken Morris, J.T. Thomas, Ralph Kaiser, Rick Nelson, Jeff Kent, Caleb Bankston, Jeremiah Wood, Keith Nale, Mike Holloway, Caleb Bankston, Ben Driebergen and Carl Boudreaux. Nice Guy: One of if not the nicest in the cast The Pratfall: At the beginning of the 11-mile hike.

characters.name: Amy O'Hara
characters.description: Determinator: See below. Officer O'Hara: She's a police seargant from Boston and her name actually is O'Hara. Handicapped Badass: Screwed up her ankle relatively early in the season. In spite of it, she kept going, actually was a force in challenges, and lasted much longer than one might expect. LadySwearsALot: According to Rites of Passage.

characters.name: Brian Corridan
characters.description: Ascended Fanboy: One of two superfans of the show this season (the other being Rafe) who have watched and studied Survivor since their youth. It can get to the point ofOne of Us. Badass Boast: (When voting for Blake) "You may be the golden boy, but I'm platinum."at hisShocking Elimination- "This is the Outwit part in Outwit, Outplay, Outlast" at hisShocking Elimination- "This is the Outwit part in Outwit, Outplay, Outlast" Graceful Loser: Brian wasn't too upset getting voted out as he was happy he went out fighting and that he was with people who were playing better than himself. Mistaken for Gay: Let's just say just that a lot of viewers thought he was gay, but he never confirmed so one way or the other.

characters.name: Margaret Bobonich
characters.description: Chekhov's Skill: Being a nurse came in handy after the first challenge: an 11-mile hike to camp. Deadpan Snarker: Especially where Judd is concerned. Once he starts ranting, she starts riffing like nobody's business. Diabolus ex Machina: The tribe switch and Judd's flipping completely put Margaret on the bottom, and a double Tribal Council twist ended up being the last straw in the mix for her career in Survivor. Team Mom: She took care of her tribe in episode 1 after the long hike and called out Judd for being a "bad sport" later on.

characters.name: Blake "Golden Boy" Towsley
characters.description: Have I Mentioned I Am Sexually Active Today?: He loved talking about both his girlfriend and his past relationships. This ended up being his downfall, as Brian came up with the "Bait Blake" strategy of encouraging Blake to constantly talk about his hookups as a way of getting the rest of his alliance to get annoyed with him and vote him out, which worked! Mr. Fanservice: A young but athletic man. Only Known by Their Nickname: "Golden Boy" Upper-Class Twit: He's hinted by the editing as being one.

characters.name: Brooke Struck
characters.description: Diabolus ex Machina: The tribe swap. According topost-game interviews, she wasin chargeat Nakúm. Afterwards, thanks to Judd flipping, she was a dead woman walking. Out of Focus: Only appeared in four episodes and had little focus.

characters.name: Brianna Varela
characters.description: Celebrity Resemblance: To Katie Holmes. The Load: Brianna was nothing but a detrimant for the Yaxhá during the third Immunity Challenge as she stood around and did nothing to help. This angered several members such as Jamie and Stephenie, and she was voted out. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: Apparently to Lydia. We hear averybrief confessional where Brianna is complaining about her, but it's never elaborated on. We Hardly Knew Ye: Only appeared in three episodes and had little focus.

characters.name: MorganMcDevitt
characters.description: Alliterative Name: Her full name is Morgan MalloyMcDevitt The Ingenue: Morgan was probably a recurrence of the SurvivorIngénuecasting archetype (Colleen Haskell being the prototype). In theSurvivor: Guatemala - TV Guide Preview, Morgan said, "I think the fact that I'm only 21, I'm the baby. The fact that I'm not set in my ways and am very open-minded, very optimistic, I think that all of those things will help." Lazy Bum: Brian and Gary claimed that Morgan was lazy around camp despite being a challenge asset, and she was the first of Yaxhá to go home because of it. Lovely Assistant: Morgan was a magician's assistant when she played Survivor and is still to this day the only person with that listed occupation. Out of Focus: Only appeared in two episodes and had little focus.

characters.name: James "Jim" Lynch
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Jim was the oldest castaway of the season and a former firefighter. Judd called him the toughest dude he ever met. Foregone Conclusion: Due to his injury and getting dehydrated from the eleven mile hike to camp, combine with his older age, it was inevitable that Jim would be out early. Jim lampshaded this in his final words, being unsurprised by his tribe's decision and the face he made when casting his vote suggested he knew his game was over. Game-Breaking Injury: Tears his bicep in the first immunity challenge, and was immediately voted out by Nakúm because of it. Old Soldier: Jim was cast for theSeasoned Veteranarchetypical role for which Rudy Boesch is the prototype. Jim is a former marine.

characters.name: La Mina
characters.description: The older men's tribe. The Artifact: Stopped being so much about "older men" and more about "the tribe that's outnumbered by a person, but is at least not constantly fighting" once the swap hit. Dwindling Party: Starting in the third episode, La Mina would go on a losing streak and ended up in the minority in the merge, and get picked off one by one. The reason the tribe wasn't completely pagonged post-merge was Terry's immunity streak. Total Party Kill: Terry's elimination meant that no one from any iteration of La Mina made to the Final Tribal Council.

characters.name: Bayoneta
characters.description: The younger women's tribe. Amazon Brigade: Bayoneta was comprised of four women. Male Gaze: Particularly, Danielle and Misty. Sally and Courtney are also good looking too. Ms. Fanservice: Everyone on the tribe. The Artifact: Like Viveros, Bayoneta disbanded at the swap despite not losing anybody.

characters.name: Viveros
characters.description: The younger men's tribe. The Artifact: Viveros and Bayoneta were removed at an early swap, but didn't actually lose any members. The Big Guy: All members were physically capable men who were well built to match. Dwindling Party: When the men started getting voted out, Viveros was quickly reduced to one member. Female Gaze: An all-men tribe of fit men? Yes.

characters.name: Casaya
characters.description: The older women's tribe. Amazon Brigade: At first. Casaya was originally formed by four older woman in the game. The Artifact: Partly because only Cirie remained by five eliminations. Partly because the "age and gender" split only lasted an episode or two.Mostlybecause their dysfunctional post-swap dynamic is better remembered. Big, Screwed-Up Family: Once the four tribes collapsed into two, they became among the most dysfunctional tribes inSurvivorhistory; but they were rather close and definitely effective. Cool Old Ladies: Invoked. The original lineup consisted of the four eldest women.

characters.name: Gitanos
characters.description: Unfortunate Names: You get the feeling nobody on the show knew "gitano" was a slur.

characters.name: Aras Baskauskas
characters.description: A yoga instructor from the original Viveros tribe, and the de facto leader of the newly formed Casaya tribe. Despite being seen by his tribe as somewhat of a ditz with questionable methods at times, Aras was perhaps the only thing keeping the most dysfunctional tribe ever put together in Survivor from splitting apart. Whether it be through mediation of the bigger personalities or a general tough challenge performance, Aras can be credited with dragging his tribe into the merge with the majority, where he then faced the problem of Terry Deitz and his impressive challenge performance, which threatened the chances of a Casaya member winning the game. Despite having numerous close shaves, and an immunity win at the Final 4 being the only thing keeping him from going home, he was saved by Danielle at the Final 3 after she won immunity and booted his arch-rival from the game. After yet another close shave after badly injuring himself during the Day 39 feast, he went on to face the jury where despite accusations of being aLazy Bum, he went on to beat Danielle in the jury vote and become the twelfthSole Survivor. Seven years and fifteen seasons later, Aras later returned to play again inBlood vs. Waterwith his brother, Vytas. Cloud Cuckoolander: Especially his method for trying to start a fire on the original Viveros tribe; it's likely that all his... eccentricities were overlooked thanks to being on the same tribe as Courtney and Shane (who were both even crazier than he was). Cool Teacher: He's a yoga instructor. He even taught Parvati Shallow yoga.

characters.name: DanielleDiLorenzo
characters.description: A medical sales representative from the original Bayoneta tribe, and one of the reasons Casaya was such a dysfunctional tribe. A competitive and aggressive person by nature, Danielle fought with Shane on what seemed like a daily basis, and it was only thanks to the efforts of Aras that she didn't actually kill him. After the merge, when the possibility of her alliance being torn apart by the challenge-dominating Terry seemed imminent, she made several decisions that saw her voting out her own alliance, including Courtney, Shane, and eventually Cirie after voting with Terry at the Final Four. However, after winning the final immunity challenge, she backstabbed Terry and saved Aras from almost certain elimination, where she went on to lose to him in the jury vote. Danielle would eventually return as one of the more questionable choices forHeroes vs. Villains. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: On the outs of her tribe largely because of this. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: By the end of the game she had betrayed quite a few close allies. The most stinging example would be Terry. Hero Killer: The last episode saw Danielle directly eliminating two major and fan favorite players this season, namely Cirie and Terry.

characters.name: Terry Deitz
characters.description: A fighter pilot from the original and switched La Mina tribe, Terry was lauded by almost everyone for his incredible physical prowess, which saw him win several key immunity challenges both pre-merge and post-merge. After La Mina went into the merge in the minority and his fellow three tribemates Nick, Austin and Sally were all voted out in succession, it was only thanks to continuous immunity wins and an over-powered Hidden Immunity Idol that he managed to worm his way far into the game, where he made an enemy of almost the entire Casaya tribe (most notably Aras), thanks to differing world views, values, and general attitude. Thanks to a late-game team-up with Danielle, he seemed almost destined to be in the finals. However, he ended up losing the final immunity challenge to Danielle, who despite promising him she would take him, sent him to the jury in 3rd place. Terry was eventually voted by the public to compete inCambodia: Second Chance. The Ace: Won many immunity challenges and outlasted all the other La Minas. His streak was so overwhelming that he managed to break up Casaya's alliance by the time he got sent home. Always Someone Better: To all of Casaya, butespeciallyto Aras. No matter what they did, Terry would always pull out immunity wins. Crippling Overspecialization: Terry is arguably the most dominant challenge competitor the show has ever seen, but he is decidedly lacking in the social and strategic components of the game.

characters.name: Cirie Fields
characters.description: A nurse from the original and switched Casaya tribe, many thought Cirie would be one of the first people booted thanks to having little to no outdoor experience (even being afraid ofleaves), and her initial position as one of the outsiders of the new Casaya tribe seemed to confirm this. However, after surviving into the merge, her adeptness of the game began to show - she managed to win a social reward challenge based on knowing her tribemates, and she even managed to orchestrate the elimination of a former tribemate at the final six by making sure every single person in the tribe voted the way she wanted them to vote, splitting the vote 3-2-1. After tucking Aras under her wing, she almost seemed like a surefire lock for the finals; however, the only thing that could possibly have screwed up her game happened at the Final 4 - Aras winning immunity. With Terry's hidden immunity idol in play, Cirie was forced into a tiebreaker with Danielle, where she narrowly lost to her former tribemate and was sent to the jury in 4th place. Being one of the fan favorites of the season, she was invited back forMicronesia: Fans vs. Favorites, and also forHeroes vs. VillainsandGame Changers. Breakout Character: Cirie easily became one of the most popular and respected castaways to play the game and won the fan favorite award at the reunion. The Everyman: A female example, personality-wise. This is especially apparent once the tribes swap and she's surrounded by extremely eccentric people on Casaya. Genius Bruiser: Is clearly a very smart player, but her being chubby doesn't help in the physical challenges. The exceptions are challenges that involve brawling, in which she easily demolishes all other female players.

characters.name: Shane Powers
characters.description: A marketing executive and single dad from Los Angeles, California. Having just stopped smoking the day before, Shane struggled with nicotine withdrawal. This was made worse by not only him ending up with Casaya, but Shane making an alliance by swearing on his son's life with the crazy people of the tribe. Shane wanted to quit, but Aras talked him out of it. Despite entering the merge with numbers, Terry's immunity streak along with an last minute change up made by Cirie at the last tribal council sent him packing at fifth. Shane was a candidate forCambodia: Second Chancebut failed to get enough votes to return. Aloof Ally: Towards Courtney and Danielle. He did pledge loyalty to them, but would frequently argue with them as well. Anti-Hero: Was a very high-strung and an unreliable contestant, but also one of the most sympathetic and least likely to backstab. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Courtney; see her entry directly below. When the two of them were left all alone, with Terry on Exile Island, Bruce evacuated out of the game, and everyone else on a reward, it sure seemed like they would get it on eventually. Instead it ended with Shane threatening to drive to her "shitty" apartment and kill her.

characters.name: Courtney Marit
characters.description: A fire dancer on the original Bayoneta. Minutes after stepping on Bayoneta, she would establish herself asquiteweird. When the first four tribes collapsed into two, she went to the notoriously dysfunctional Casaya, and became a strong reason for its reputation. Courtney soon aligned with Shane, an equally odd fellow, with whom she would often butt heads with. Although the merge was initially smooth sailing, Terry's immunity streak would force the former Casayas to turn on each other. Courtney decided to align with Terry. However, Cirie, deeming her the biggest threat because she would go to the final two, arranged for her ouster and Courtney got voted out in 6th place. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Her tribemates openly suspected that her tempestuous relationship with Shane was covering for a crush. Although in this case, it's theguywho has the sudden mood swings. When Courtney and Shane were left all alone, with Terry on Exile Island, Bruce evacuated out of the game, and everyone else on a reward, it sure seemed like they would get it on eventually. Instead it ended with Shane threatening to drive to her "shitty" apartment and kill her. Butt-Monkey: She gets mocked by most the rest of the cast and this is exemplified in The Touchy Subjects challenge. Cassandra Truth/Dumbass Has a Point: In her argument with Aras, Courtney points out if Terry has the idol he would not give it up. Considering the idol at the time was usedafterthe votes were revealed, this was a reasonable assumption. Plus, she was right in the end as Terry did not use it on anyone. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Her somewhat oblivious nature combined with her focus on alternative spirituality gives this impression.

characters.name: Bruce Kanegai
characters.description: A martial arts instructor and art teacher placed on the original La Mina. After the elimination of Melinda, he was placed on Casaya, where he was pegged as an outsider. He was nearly voted out in episode five due to a conflict with Aras, but was saved by Danielle's lobbying. When the tribes merged, the former La Mina attempted to Bruce to flip, but he didn't budge. He kept steady rather far into the game, before being evacuated due to severe constipation. Badass Bookworm: An old schoolteacher who held his own until sickness forced him out. Butt-Monkey: Bruce was exiled twice consecutively and was eventually removed from the game in a painful way. Cool Old Guy: Mostly liked and respected by the tribe, despite his occasional crabbiness and wine-stealing. Cool Teacher: Both a martial arts instructor and an art teacher.

characters.name: Sally Schumann
characters.description: A social worker on the Bayoneta tribe. Once she became on La Mina, Sally would become an outsider with Misty's blindside. She was exiled in the sixth episode, which saved her from certain elimination. When the merge happen, Sally's luck didn't improve and she was eventually voted out in 8th place as part of Casaya's pagonging. Born Unlucky/Butt-Monkey: Sally was consistently in the minority since Day 8. Ms. Fanservice: A very pretty young woman withZettai Ryouiki. Shout-Out: She wears her hair inPrincess Leiabuns during the Final Tribal Council. The Smurfette Principle: Sally very quickly became the last woman standing once Casaya started their winning streak.

characters.name: Austin Carty
characters.description: A writer on the Viveros tribe. When switched to La Mina, Austin would join Terry and Dan to form a men's alliance. However, La Mina's losing streak cost them the numbers advantages. Because of Terry's immunity streak and not using his hidden immunity idol, Austin was voted out in 9th. Informed Attribute: Austin claimed he can't help butflirt with women. We don't see that and he even chose to be in a men's alliance over one with two beautiful women. Nice Guy: His comforting of Sally over her rough relationship with her parents stands out. Wounded Gazelle Gambit: Enacted one at the first individual immunity challenge to avoid being voted out.

characters.name: Nick Stanbury
characters.description: An accountant on the Viveros tribe. When transferred to La Mina, Nick was on the men's alliance. Unlike his friend, Austi, Nick was much quieter a contestant. However, La Mina entered the merge without numbers in their side and no alliance to support them. When Terry won immunity, Nick was voted out for being the next-biggest threat. Heroic Build: Nick might not be a full blownMr. Fanservicebut he has some amazing abs. Last Words: Instead of the usual pleasantries or bitter rants people give when they are voted off, Nick gives a strangely profound motivational speech:All you kids in your mid 20s that are in my situation, confused, not sure which direction life's pulling you, you're just trying to find yourself. I urge us all, please, be hungry, be foolish, block out the noise, find yourselves, be who you potentially are, and be true to your dreams, and what you really want to do. If we all maximize that personal freedom, then we'll change the world. Out of Focus: Nick was a quieter character who didn't have much a role beyond being in an alliance with Terry. The Stoic: Best example is when Sally lost the spear. He kept calm and told the panicky Sally that everything is going to be okay.

characters.name: Dan Barry
characters.description: A retired astronaut who was originally placed on La Mina. He immediately befriended Terry based on flying backgrounds. After the switch, Dan was in a comfortable men's alliance. In the last pre merge immunity challenge, Dan fouled up, costing his tribe the win. With the usual target, Sally, on Exile Island, Dan was voted instead. Cool Old Guy: He's almost universally liked by his tribemates. Graceful Loser: Accepts his vote-out and states he was just grateful to have another adventure. Retired Badass: He's a former astronaut. His tribe certainly respected him enough to think of him as this.

characters.name: Bobby "Bobdawg" Mason
characters.description: An attorney from the original Viveros tribe and the newly formed Casaya tribe. Bobby, or "Bobdawg" as he's better known outside of the show, is best known outside of Survivor for his commentary surrounding the show and how early boots such as himself are portrayed. Unfortunately for him, he was also stuck on Casaya, one of the most dysfunctional tribes ever assembled, where he was forced to deal with people who not only wanted to vote him out; but also some legitimately crazy people. After going off on Courtney for annoying him over a bottle of wine that he drank with Bruce, plus the possibility of him flipping over to La Mina at the merge looming, he was voted out by the women of Casaya in 12th place. Ascended Fanboy: He wasbarely shownduring his season, but absolutely a textbook case. Check out histhreadon Survivor Sucks where he speaks about his experiences on the show and why the editing screwed him over. It's surprisingly insightful. Advertised Extra: Despite his early exit, Bobby was featured on the cover for the Panama DVD. Badass Boast: Describes his starting tribe (the younger men) as the "young beefcake crowd," and describes himself as the charter member and president. Genius Bruiser: A very strong man and an intelligent attorney, though his intelligence was not shown much on camera.

characters.name: Ruth Marie Milliman
characters.description: Real estate agent from the original Casaya tribe and the newly formed La Mina tribe. While she was initially branded as a strong competitor by her tribemates thanks to winning the first reward challenge, she was less well-received on La Mina thanks to the prominence of the all-guy alliance, and was sent home in 13th place after being perceived as weak. Cool Old Lady: She was one who won the older women the first challenge. The tribe respected her judging by the voting confessionals. Full-Name Basis: Always "Ruth Marie", never "Ruth". Girlish Pigtails: Very feminine and wears her hair in two small braids. Graceful Loser: In her post-elimination interview during the recap episode, she says she was lied to and deceived, but she doesn’t blame anyone because that’s the name of the game.

characters.name: Misty Giles
characters.description: A missile engineer and former beauty queen from the original Bayonetta tribe. The first person to ever be sent to Exile Island, Misty was sent to the newly formed La Mina tribe after the swap, where she ended up being the first target of the all-guy alliance and sent home in 14th place. The Charmer: Attempted to work the younger men and failed. I Coulda Been a Contender!: Terry's explanation for getting rid of her is that she was too intelligent to keep around. In addition, her elimination arguably contributed to beginning La Mina’s losing streak. Ms. Fanservice: A very beautiful woman, and she tried (and failed) to use it to her advantage.
